Mydei is supposed to be here to celebrate. After so much hard work he and his band—Titans of Calamity, had finally signed a recording contract. The last person he wanted to run into was him. Popular, handsome, up-and-coming model Phainon, who had become unrecognizable from the boy he loved in high school. Mydei never got over their disastrous breakup, and right now, he just wants to forget. But Phainon won’t make it easy for him.

Chapter 1: You Were My Favourite

Chapter Summary

Phainon leans closer to him, unaware of the way Mydei’s breath hitches when he goes nearer. “Let’s find a time and place to do ‘it’ later.” he whispers.

Mydei completely freezes in his seat, and then in a low, gruff voice like he is trying very hard to hold himself back, asks “Do ‘it’?”

Phainon blinks at him innocently, not understanding why he’s giving such a strange reaction. “You know, to wrestle.”

Mydei shuts his eyes and gives a long, drawn-out sigh. He does not open them again for a long time.

chapters.html:
Mydei has been blessed with a lot of advantages in life. Loving parents, financial security, a warm roof to grow up under, and he’s not bad looking if he does say so himself. But as a teenager in high school, he did not have any friends. Not a single one.

Because he stood out, and not in the good kind of way. He was too tall, too intimidating, all muscles and long limbs and face etched in a permanent scowl. His wardrobe didn’t help his case either, he frequently got into trouble for violating the uniform dress code: His collared white shirt was never tucked in, and always worn open to reveal the black t-shirt underneath. He wore earrings, which were against school regulations, and always wore a thin, dangling gold chain around his neck. He thought it looked cool, but to the other students, he was obviously trouble on two legs, a possible gang member, even.

The other students looked away when he skulked down the corridors, gave his desk a large berth in class so they wouldn’t have to pass him, and panicked when it was time to divide themselves into groups because who’d want to do a group project with a delinquent, are you crazy?

All except one guy.

All except Phainon.

“Hi.” The white-haired boy said, cheerfully plopping his schoolbag on the empty seat opposite Mydei. “I need a project partner. You need a project partner. What do you say?”

Mydei raises an eyebrow. It’s not that he doesn’t appreciate the forwardness, but the other students are still assigning themselves, so it’s not like he’s short on options. Phainon is the smartest guy in their class, he’s sure the other students would love to be his partner. There is no benefit to teaming up with Mydei, so he can’t help but question his sanity.

“Did you lose a bet or something?” He asks blandly. Not that he cares, but he simply doesn’t want to deal with the inconvenience of Phainon regretting his decision later and flaking out.

Because he’ll end up doing twice the work, and that just sucks all around.

Phainon just peers at him over his thick-rimmed glasses. “No?” He sounds almost offended. “I made my own decision to approach you, what, you don’t want to be my partner? You dislike me that much?”

“I don’t even know you.” Mydei points out. He doesn’t waste energy disliking people, he simply takes the path of least resistance and avoids people he doesn’t care about. Since most of the student body already didn't like him, he hadn’t bothered to get to know them either. Why should he, when they wouldn’t extend him the same courtesy?

“Ouch, you know, that kind of hurts. I’ve been in your class for the whole year.” Phainon smiles ruefully. “But better late than never, right? Why don’t we get to know each other?”

And that was how Phainon wormed his way into his life.

They made an unlikely pair. Phainon was Mydei’s opposite in every way, with his nerdy glasses, messy, thick white hair, and dopey smile. He was always wearing an oversized sweater over his uniform that draped over him like a poncho. He was polite and meek and soft spoken and disappeared during lunch break to go play whatever game he brought to school on his handheld console, alone.

And then all of a sudden he was no longer alone, because Mydei started joining him.

He hadn’t planned on becoming Phainon’s friend outside of class too, but he saw him completely forget to eat his lunch once because he was so engrossed with his game. And if there’s anything Mydei can’t stand, it’s to see someone skipping meals. So he shoves his own lunch into Phainon’s hands, because Kephale forbid his project partner passes out from hunger.

Mydei isn’t a big gamer either but he does own a console and sometimes he can’t stop himself from looking over Phainon’s shoulder and making snarky comments at how he’s playing his game. This normally leads to Phainon huffing, shoving the console at him and going “Then let’s see you do better, smart ass,” and it’s not his fault he’s easily baited by challenges.

“The other students think I’m bullying you,” Mydei says one day. It’s a very understandable conclusion, given the uh… stereotypes. It’s not that Mydei cares about what other people say, but he still has ears, and it’s tough to avoid the rumours.

“Maybe I should stop hanging out with you,” he continues. Because unlike Mydei, Phainon is well-liked among the student body. He is nerdy, sweet, a teacher’s pet, and always willing to lend a helping hand to others. Being seen around Mydei so often will only tarnish his reputation.

“Huh, why?” That makes Phainon look up from his game, blue eyes blown wide with alarm. Combined with his glasses, it makes them look unbelievably huge, like a bug.

“Didn’t you hear what I said? They think I’m beating you up!” Mydei explains, annoyed again.

It’s unfortunately true that Mydei gets into fights a lot, and he doesn’t bother to conceal the scrapes or bruises he sometimes comes to school with. For some reason, especially among the Kremnoans, people thought he was strong, and lined up in droves to challenge him. And well, there is no word for ‘backing down from a challenge’ in the Kremnoan dictionary.

It’s just self-defense, but that makes people more convinced that he’s a brute.

It doesn’t even make sense, if he was beating up Phainon, wouldn’t Phainon be the one with bruises, and not Mydei?

Phainon just laughs at his frustration. “Haha! I’m afraid I’ll have to disappoint you. I’m not so easy to beat up even if you wanted to.”

Mydei rolls his eyes. Phainon with his oversized sweater and dorky glasses is absolutely an easy target, even if he’s in denial. “I’m not going to do anything to you. You don’t have to act tough around me.”

“I’m not acting tough!” Phainon sulks. “Why don’t you wrestle me, right here, right now?”

“Are you crazy?” They’re sitting inside a discussion room in the library. It’s one of the few places to get some peace and quiet around here, and avoid the gawks of the other students. “We’re still inside the school, dumbass. What’s it going to look like if people see me beating you up in real time?”

At that, Phainon laughs so hard that his eyes crinkle into crescents and he has to hunch over because his stomach hurts. “I don’t think you can!” He finally says in between peals of mocking laughter. “Though you’re most welcome to try.”

Mydei tilts his head, an amused smirk dancing across his face. This nerd is not as meek as he appears, and has quite the smart mouth.

“I’m curious now… but I really shouldn’t. I can’t get suspended again.” Not like it was his fault the first time, since the other guy started it. But the look on his parent’s faces was so devastating that he can’t risk it happening again.

Come to think of it, he can’t blame the other students for giving him such a bad rep, since he has the history for it too…

“Uh… then… for now, let’s arm wrestle!” Phainon suggests.

“Okay, that’s acceptable.”

Mydei places his elbow on the table, flexing his arm in a way that makes the veins on his forearms pop. He doesn’t mean to brag, but he’s been lifting weights lately and his parents even built him a little home gym to workout in. It’s completely understandable if Phainon gets intimidated.

Except that he’s the one shocked when Phainon rolls up the sleeves of his oversized sweater. Instead of a skinny noodle arm, he’s greeted with muscle. Engorged veins trace the back of Phainon’s hand, running up his forearm and disappearing under his sleeve. When he curls his fingers into a fist, the muscles beneath the skin contract in a very visible way.

Mydei swallows and realizes he’s staring.

“I’m impressed. Maybe you’ll be a challenge after all.” Mydei says, trying to cover up his flusteredness with bravado.

Still, there was nobody who could beat Mydei at his own game. This will be an easy win.

They clasp their hands together, Phainon’s palm warm against his as they count down from three. On the mark, Mydei pushes down immediately with all his strength, expecting to slam Phainon’s arm onto the table in seconds.

But their entwined hands do not budge.

Phainon’s strength is equal to his, something Mydei has never experienced before. He’s not winning, damn, he’s not even moving.

Mydei can’t help but meet Phainon’s eyes, not knowing whether he should be feeling impressed or irritated, perhaps a mixture of both. At least he’s not making it easy for Phainon, because the veins on his forehead are bulging as he resists Mydei with all his might.

“Not bad Mydeimos! You’re pretty strong.” Phainon says. Even talking a little distracts him and Mydei gains just a little bit of leeway before their strengths even out again.

“Haha,” Mydei can’t help but bark out a laugh, gritting his teeth. “Not too bad yourself.”

Their arms interlock for a long time, contesting in a silent battle of wills, until Mydei finally manages to overpower Phainon with sheer endurance. It's a narrower win than he’d like, one that could have gone either way, depending on the day.

“How does a nerd that spends all their free time reading books or playing video games get so built anyway?” Mydei asks, having to shake out his arm to get rid of the pins and needles. Damn, his muscles are going to be sore tomorrow.

“Well, before I moved to Okhema, my parents owned a farm. I’ve been lifting heavy objects and helping in the fields since I was young! Even now I get antsy if I don’t exercise every day.”

Mydei can’t help but give Phainon a once over. He doesn’t look it because his posture is awful and he has a baby face, but he’s as tall as Mydei, who is not short in any sense of the word. Plus sometimes when he shifts and his sweater stretches over his shoulders it reveals the faint but undeniable lines of the musculature underneath.

It really makes Mydei wonder what he might look like underneath those baggy clothes.

“If you like to exercise, why don’t you join a sports team? That could increase your popularity among the other students too.” Mydei suggests.

“I don’t know, I rather spend my free time doing other stuff.” Phainon shrugs. “Why do I need to increase my popularity, anyway?”

“So… you won’t be on your own all the time.” Mydei says, it's an obvious answer. After all, nobody likes being lonely.

“I’m not lonely, aren’t I? I got you.”

Play stupid games, win stupid prizes. Mydei’s brain short circuits and he feels heat rise to his face. Does Phainon even realize the things he’s saying and how it might be taken the wrong way? All of a sudden, he realizes how close they’re sitting, and how he can still feel the warmth of Phainon’s palm on his.

Since he caught Phainon forgetting to eat that one time, Mydei had taken the initiative to bring double the lunches. One for himself and one to shove into Phainon’s hands to guilt him into having his meals.

Plus, the delighted look on his friend’s face whenever he opens the lunchbox to see what’s on the menu is never boring.

“Should we take turns bringing each other lunches?” Phainon asks, stuffing his face with the homemade sushi Mydei brought them today. “I feel bad that your mom is always cooking for me. I can make a pretty mean salad!”

“It’s alright. My mom’s not the one making the lunches.” Mydei says, digging into his own meal.

Phainon stops eating.

Mydei glances up too. “What?”

“Are you buying them? Mydei, you bring lunch for me almost everyday! You can’t spend that kind of money on me!” Phainon protests, eyes growing wide and panicked at the mere idea.

Mydei just rolls his eyes. “Relax, I made them.”

Phainon just blinks at him. “You… make these lunches? Everyday?”

Not long after he had gotten into bodybuilding and nutrition, Mydei realized that preparing and cooking his own healthy meals became a source of relaxation and enjoyment for him.

“Yes, making a little extra for you is no trouble at all.” Mydei says, hoping that puts the matter to rest.

“Oh, wow. You’re ama—I mean, that’s amazing!!!” Phainon stumbles over his words with a nervous laugh. “I didn’t know you could cook so well. I feel embarrassed now, cause some of my compliments were uhm… a little excessive.”

Mydei just scoffs. Phainon had moaned so loudly eating the lasagne he brought last week that it lingered in Mydei’s mind for days. But he doesn’t mind, it feels nice having someone praise his cooking so sincerely.

“Don’t worry about it. I think any chef would be happy that their cooking was enjoyed.”

“Then I’ll be sure to continue!” Phainon grins, eating with renewed gusto. “Man, you’re so cool, you’re strong, and you’re a great chef as well! Is there anything you’re not good at?”

Heat rises up his neck again, Mydei had never received such glowing praise on his character before and it was a little embarrassing. “It’s not a big deal… cooking is just a hobby.”

“Oh,” Phainon rolls his eyes as though to say ‘get a load of this guy’. “Any other hobbies I should know about, then?”

Now he’s really feeling shy, Mydei redirects his gaze, staring hard at the wall as he quietly admits. “I also like… baking, and singing… and playing the guitar.”

He knows they’re not the most masculine of hobbies, or hobbies that people expected a guy like him to have. And Phainon’s reaction reflects that as his eyebrows shoot straight up.

“Wow. I didn’t know our scary Mydeimos had such adorable hobbies!”

Phainon, with his big blue eyes, thick glasses, chubby cheeks, and fluffy overgrown white hair looks like an angel. But Mydei is convinced that he’s actually a devil, or at least a professional ragebaiter. Someone who has a phD in testing Mydei’s patience.

“I’m not cute!” He manages to choke out incredulously.

“I’d like to point out that’s a very cute response.”

“Shut up!” Mydei says with no venom. He likes his scary reputation, likes that it keeps others at arm’s length from him. Likes that his so-called ‘cute’ side is one that only Phainon knows. He wants to keep it that way. “You better not tell anyone.”

“Why would I when I get to keep your cute expressions all to myself?” Phainon says smugly. Mydei flushes even harder at how well he has echoed his thoughts, and thinks that the nerd is not as harmless as he appears.

“Gimme your homework.” Mydei demands, dropping his bag on the floor in front of Phainon’s desk, causing him to startle.

It’s a free period right now, Phainon’s time to catch up on his reading or revise like a responsible student, and Mydei’s time to speed run all his homework so that he can spend the rest of his evening in peace. It’s unusual to see Mydei so panicked, because he’s normally very on top of his schoolwork, to the point where he’s normally the one sending Phainon the reminders.

Mydei’s face is dour. It must be a desperate situation if he’s asking to copy Phainon’s homework.

“Is this some kind of bully-nerd roleplay?” Phainon asks, because he can’t resist getting a jab in.

Mydei’s eyes widen when he realizes what it looks like to the other students. It’s very cute. The idea that he could bully Phainon is quite laughable, to be honest. People who judge others on appearances alone are pathetic.

“What? No, I really need your help!” Mydei pleads.

Phainon puts his chin in his palm, grinning at Mydei cheekily. “I don’t know, I was pretty scared earlier. Maybe if you said ~please~.”

Mydei scowls at him. He rarely gets this stressed out about anything, so Phainon has to conclude that it must be related to math, his worst subject. He knows that Mydei’s parents had been threatening to send him for math tutoring if his grades drop any further, which was a fate worse than death for him.

Mydei sinks into the empty chair opposite Phainon and grabs the edge of the table, like he’s bracing himself. Phainon beams at him with his sunniest smile as he waits for it. Mydei takes a deep breath in and, in a voice so soft and rough that Phainon didn’t even know he was capable of it, begs:

“Please, Phainon.”

The way in which he said it would stick in Phainon’s memories for years to come. His own smirk falters, and he blinks rapidly as a faint heat creeps up his neck. He has to subtly adjust the collar of his shirt so that it’s not visible.

Mydei is definitely doing this just to fuck with him, but he doesn’t know the affect he has on him. Phainon has secretly admired him for ages now before getting the courage to talk to him.

He has to stop his hands from trembling as he reaches for his bag.

“Okay, okay, just take it!” Phainon doesn’t know which homework Mydei wants, so he just takes them all out, laying them across the table like an offering.

Mydei wastes no time in making a grab for the math worksheet—he knew it, Mydei’s so predictable—nearly flipping his own bag upside down in his haste to find his homework to start copying. As he upturns his bag, various things flutter to the floor, pencils, notebooks, random sheets of paper.

Phainon reaches his hand and grabs one lone piece of paper before it can hit the floor. When he flips it over, he finds that it’s just doodles of red symbols and markings, some jagged like lighting bolts, others swirling like ripples in a lake.

He squints at it, clearly not able to make heads or tails of it. A foreign language? He wasn’t aware that any had an alphabet like this.

“Mydei, what’s this?” He asks.

Across the table, Mydei barely glances up, too busy copying his answers with the speed of a man about to fail his classes. Despite his delinquent exterior his penmanship is surprisingly neat, clean letters with an almost flowy elegance to them.

“Some ideas for tattoos I want to get once I turn 18.” He says simply.

“So many?” The entire paper is filled with sketches. If Mydei gets all of these tattooed on himself, he’ll be inked from head to toe.

The idea of Mydei’s already quite beautiful body decorated with vivid red markings is making Phainon’s head want to explode.

“Tattoos are significant in Kremnoan culture, my parents have plenty of their own. Historically, they represented the spirit and courage of warriors, and are a mark of pride and victory.”

Mydei pauses for just a moment, before a small smile curls the corner of his mouth.

“Also, I just like tattoos.”

“I think they would look good on you.” Phainon praises, he means it.

They continue working in silence, Mydei slowly filling out his worksheet with Phainon’s answers, brow furrowed in concentration. Phainon tries to return to his own revision, he really does, but his eyes wander to Mydei more often than not. He can’t help it, he’d known he was attracted to guys for quite some time now, and after some self reflection has pinned down what he considers to be his ‘type’.

And to be honest, Mydei ticks all the boxes. He’s handsome, strong, cool, clever, and hides a surprisingly soft side behind that delinquent exterior.

At first Phainon had only approached him with the intention of being friends, but now he’s forced to admit that he might have a crush on the guy.

He watches the way Mydei’s forearm flexes as he writes, remembering the time they arm wrestled in the library. Mydei had won, but it was close. It would have been better if they actually went all out, pitting their full strength against each other, but Mydei had been against it at the time. And well, if he used his full strength they might have broken the table, and that would have been bad.

Phainon always liked that kind of thing, pitting his strength against someone else, seeing who came up on top. Growing up in Aedes Elysiae, he’d been like any other village kid, he loved roughhousing in the fields with other children. But as he continued to grow, his strength rapidly outpaced that of the other kids and he was forced to stop because he could accidentally hurt them, even if he hadn’t meant to. He learned that lesson the hard way.

So Phainon learned to wrap himself up in soft fabric to make himself seem harmless.

But sometimes, the way Mydei looks at him seems to hint that he sees through Phainon’s exterior.

He wonders what it would be like to fight him for real.

“Mydei, do you remember that conversation we had last time?”

Mydei just looks at him like he’s the biggest idiot in the world. “Explain properly, I can’t read your mind.”

“You know, that day when we arm wrestled and I said you couldn’t beat me up even if you tried.”

Mydei’s hand pauses, and he clears his throat nervously until he speaks again. The small gesture slips past Phainon, unnoticed. “I remember, also… I could definitely beat you up.”

Still not backing down, so stubborn. But that’s kind of what Phainon likes about him. Mydei doesn’t go easy on someone just because they look meek.

Phainon leans closer to him, unaware of the way Mydei’s breath hitches when he goes nearer. “Let’s find a time and place to do ‘it’ later.” he whispers.

Phainon blinks at him innocently, not understanding why he’s giving such a strange reaction. “You know, to wrestle.”

Mydei shuts his eyes and gives a long, drawn-out sigh. He does not open them again for a long time.

“Yes, of course. To wrestle. That was also my thought process.”

“That doesn’t sound too convincing to me. Tell me, what was really going through your mind?” Phainon flutters his eyelashes innocently, he knows that he’s playing with fire, but Mydei is just too fun to mess with.

Mydei’s response is to immediately push him away in the most dastardly way possible, by rubbing his fingertips against the lenses of Phainon’s glasses.

Phainon gapes behind his now smudged vision, stunned into silence by the barbarism.

“You monster!”

“Let’s find a time and place to do ‘it’ later.” The mere memory of Phainon’s words is enough to send heat rising up Mydei’s face.

Of course, he gets horny like any other teenager, but those problems are easily resolved with his hand and pictures of some of the athletes on the sports magazines his father likes to buy.

He’d never felt this way over any other boy before, and it feels like he’s a little too old to talk to his parents about getting his first crush. So Mydei tries to just deal with it on his own.

But the idea of sparring with Phainon starts to become more and more appealing. He’s always wondered what Phainon’s body will feel like over his… in a totally bro way, of course. And was also curious about the sleeper build he seemed to carry underneath his baggy clothes… in a most platonic way, naturally. Mydei: About our spar… There is a boxing gym near my house that I sometimes visit. It’s spacious and quiet and we won’t get interrupted. How about we wrestle there?

Phainon: That sounds great!!! Just tell me the time and date and I’ll be there. I can’t wait! <3

He was so full of hidden surprises that Mydei was proud to be one of the very few people who knew the real Phainon. Who knew the sharp, slightly aggressive, playful, competitive boy behind the glasses who wanted to test his mettle against a worthy opponent.

Plus, he can’t say he’s not a little curious as to what strength he might be hiding.

Phainon keeps sneaking glances at him from the other side of the classroom, but Mydei, out of pettiness, ignores him. Every now and again, his phone buzzes with texts from his desperate boyfriend.

Is he Mydei’s boyfriend still?

It feels like he doesn’t know him. Did he ever?

Why did he feel the need to make such a drastic change and why did Mydei seem like the last person to find out.

He doesn’t know anything.

Once Mydei had a chance to cool down and get over his shock, his reaction did seem a little over the top. He convinces himself there must be a good reason Phainon is acting this way, even if he doesn’t understand it yet. A face to face conversation would do well to clear these misunderstandings up and get them back on track again.

Mydei misses him, had missed him the whole summer. He didn’t expect to come back to this

Unfortunately, despite his promises to explain everything later, ‘later’ became far too vague for Mydei’s liking. Phainon was suddenly popular, he was swarmed by fellow students like they were bees and he was the most fragrant flower in the garden. Whenever Mydei thought he saw his chance, someone else had already hooked their arm through his and was pulling him along to whatever they had planned that day.

And what was utterly baffling was that Phainon just went along with it.

He didn’t protest or fight back, he smiled, nodded politely and played the part.

The first time it happened Mydei just stood there, staring in bewilderment, because the Phainon he knew was so fiercely independent that he was even opposed to joining a sports team because he would rather be spending his free time doing something else.

It was a quality that Mydei admired about him.

Now he shares his time so freely and sincerely with everybody else.

But once Mydei had made up his mind that he was going to be understanding, going to give Phainon a chance to explain himself, then he was going to stick with it no matter how much his instincts raged at him to put his walls back up.

“Mydei!” After what had seemed like a long, drawn-out battle, he finally cornered Phainon alone on the emergency stairs of the school, the place they used to claim as theirs. Phainon turns around as he approaches and gives him a blinding grin, the kind that he thought used to be reserved for him alone, but now seems to be given freely to everyone.

“I’m sorry-” Were the first words out of his mouth.

Mydei drops his bag, sighing deeply.

“I don’t want to hear your apologies.” He interrupts. Phainon immediately shuts his mouth, eyebrows furrowing in concern. “I’ll decide what to do once I hear you out, so talk.”

Phainon still has that kicked puppy look on his face, he looks pathetic.

“It all started when Caenis called me into her office before summer break. I think… that was the first time I realized how hard things were for you in this school.”

Mydei’s frown deepens. “I never thought that things were difficult for me. Stop making assumptions.” It was simply the hand he was dealt, and he did

what he could with it. Mydei even thought he was fairly lucky, all things considered.

“Well, I hated it. I hated how you were treated, and I hated how I couldn’t do anything for you.”

“I never asked you to-”

“Mydei, please.” Phainon pleads, and Mydei’s jaw clamps shut as he grimly nods to him to continue.

“I thought, if I was more popular, more well-liked, someone with authority, I could change things, I could protect you.”

Mydei’s face twitches because he’s dying to say something. It’s offensive that Phainon thinks he’s a damsel in distress who needs protection, it’s hurtful that Phainon went ahead with his own plans before even consulting Mydei on what he thinks of the situation. It’s ironic that Phainon’s attempts to help him have made him more lonely and isolated in return.

“That’s why I’m running for student council president… I wanted to tell you that.” Phainon punctuates it with a shaky laugh. “It’s the only way to make any lasting changes around here. And that’s why I’m acting like this… can’t make an omelette without breaking a few eggs, right?”

Mydei’s jaw shifts, his voice is low and guttural as he manages to whisper out. “Since when have you ever cared about stuff like that?”

“Since I started caring about you.” Phainon answers honestly.

Mydei is conflicted, because if Phainon’s intentions are pure, and he is truly doing this because he cares for Mydei, then why does it hurt him so much?

He should feel grateful that his boyfriend is going through such lengths, but instead he just feels… left behind.

But if this is something Phainon wants to do, however misguided it may seem, then Mydei would support him. He tells himself he can live with that, he’d always been a bit of a backstage assistant than someone who prefers to

be in the spotlight anyway. And he’s not so shallow as to change the way he feels about Phainon because he looks a little different. Mydei likes to think that he’s a better man than that.

So he really does try.

He plays the role of a supportive boyfriend with quiet diligence. He bakes cupcakes for Phainon’s campaign, though the credit ultimately goes to some of the girls because he can’t stand behind the booth to sell them, still aware of the bad image he holds among the student body. He continues bringing Phainon nutritious lunches, because the guy would forget to eat with how busy he is lately. And whenever he sees campaign posters peeling from the walls or displaced in some shape or form, he carefully presses them back into place—even though one time he got accused of vandalism. He tries not to let meaningless things like that bother him.

But the longer this goes on the harder it becomes to accept that this is something he has to be okay with.

Instead of feeling proud of how his boyfriend seems to shine so brightly, he just seems to feel a deep, profound emptiness inside.

Like this world Phainon is building isn’t one meant for him.

“Listen, I know you haven’t gotten the appreciation you deserve.” Phainon says, holding him by the hands when they’re alone, because of course, now he only touches Mydei when there’s nobody around to see. “But it’ll all get better once I become student council president. I’ll make real changes, I promise.”

Of course he will, Mydei hears that line in every one of his presidential campaign speeches while standing silently at the back.

It’s becoming harder for Mydei to just overlook how different he is from the Phainon he knows. How he’s become someone who has to speak so carefully because of the way he’d be perceived, who has to carry himself with dignity and poise at all times, who has to put on a mask to meet everyone else’s expectations, balanced on his shoulders.

It can’t be easy for him, and that’s why it hurts Mydei even more. Because Phainon seems willing to bear everyone else’s dreams except Mydei’s extremely simple ones.

The hopes that they’ll remain exactly as they are.

“Phainon,” Mydei asks, a last ditch effort to get him to abandon this folly. “If I said I didn’t want things to change. Would you listen?”

Phainon hesitates. “But—I’m really close to achieving my goal.” he says, voice quietly confident. “If I stop now, then we’ll get nowhere at all. I need to protect you, remember?”

Mydei’s jaw tightens, he has a feeling that they’ve been getting nowhere for some time now. Phainon’s stubbornness, something he had once admired, was now being used against him.

“I’m sorry, I didn’t realize dating me has been such a burden to you.” He lets bitterness get the best of him, speaking between gritted teeth. He’s been enduring it silently for some time now, but even his patience had its limits.

“What?” Phainon blurts out, surprised by his sudden venom. Sometimes it feels like they’re walking on parallel tracks, close enough to see each other, but never to intersect. “That’s not what I meant. Let’s think of it this way, uhm, if I could shield you like a tree-”

Mydei’s glare sharpens. “Stop talking in metaphors and speak plainly. Why do you keep asking as though I’m someone that needs to be shielded?”

“I thought you would understand.” Phainon dodges the question, frustration slipping into his tone.

“I would understand,” Mydei starts, his temper flaring up for real this time. “If you bothered speaking to me like your boyfriend instead of reciting poetry when I ask you a simple question.”

Phainon’s jaw clamps shut, a clouded expression in his eyes. Mydei wonders if he’s going to back off or fight back, gods, he hopes Phainon

fights back. He wants to argue, wants to throw fists, wants to see that fire in his eyes again to know that he is not lost yet.

But instead, at the worst timing, Phainon’s phone rings.

Phainon only needs to take one look at the screen before his expression scrunches into that stupid apologetic one that Mydei is starting to really hate.

“I’m so sorry Mydei, I have to go.”

“You have to go?” He repeats mockingly. “I waited weeks to talk to you and you can’t spare half an hour?”

Phainon just sighs, his entire shoulders shifting downwards as though Mydei just doesn’t understand. “It’s a student council election strategy meeting. Some of the debate club members have agreed to help me with my campaign, and they can only meet now.”

Mydei feels something in him die. The fire is extinguished in just a snap.

“Right, can’t have anything risking the campaign.”

Phainon knows he’s being sarcastic, if his sheepish expression is any indication.

Mydei just storms away, having nothing else to say. He feels a headache coming on. He hated when people did that, speaking in riddles, in ways that made it harder to grasp their true intentions. He always thought that Phainon wouldn’t do that to him.

He thought he was the person who understood Phainon better than anyone, and vice versa.

Seems like they didn’t understand each other at all.

Phainon wins the student council election by a landslide, of course he does, because Mydei knows he can do anything he sets his mind to. “The

committee members are throwing me a celebration party! You should come! I’ll introduce you to everyone.” Phainon says with sparkles in his eyes.

“I’ll think about it,” Mydei says, knowing he has no intention of showing up.

He spends that weekend moping at home instead, feeling like he’s losing all the parts of Phainon that he loved, like sand slipping through his fingers.

The worst part about it is that Phainon has never looked happier. Laughing, smiling, chatting to other people, sharing his warmth and kindness with other people who are not Mydei. The fact that Mydei is still latching on to him for happiness must be a burden.

It’s him that needs Phainon too much.

Phainon is like the sun, but the sun didn’t only belong to one person. The sun shines for everyone. And the sooner Mydei accepted that, the better.

He makes up his mind and texts Phainon.

Mydei: Can we meet up tonight? I know it’s out of the blue. There’s something important I want to talk about.

Phainon: Haha, did you have to say it so ominously? I’m gonna think you’re trying to break up with me or something

Mydei: … Don’t overthink it. I think it’s better for us to talk in person.

Maybe Phainon does realize what’s coming next, because he tries his hardest to deter Mydei from what he actually wants to say when they meet.

“We missed you at the celebration party, I missed you.” Phainon immediately makes a grab for his hand as soon as he shows up. Mydei

angles his hand just slightly so he misses, but Phainon notices, of course he does, and hurt flits across his face for just a second before he plasters on a bright smile.

“I’m really sorry I couldn’t make it for a date last weekend.” He apologizes. “There was a student council bowling event and I needed to be there.”

“It’s fine.” Mydei says a little numbly, he’s lost count of how many times Phainon has been too busy for him.

“But look, now that the election is over I have some free time. Why don’t we go on a date tomorrow, just you and me? I’ll treat you to that dessert place you like.” Phainon’s actually trying so hard that it makes Mydei feel a little guilty, but he’s made up his mind already, and nothing will change it.

Mydei just huffs. “It’s okay, save your money.”

“What good is having money if I can’t treat my boyfriend to something nice?”

And if Phainon is too cowardly to approach the inevitable, then Mydei will do so for him.

“I think this relationship is not going to work out,” Mydei says plainly. “I want to break up.”

“What?” Phainon is still smiling, but it’s trembling at the edges, brittle. He looks like he wants to break at any moment, yet, that stupid smile stays on. Mydei wishes he’d show any kind of emotion at all, to cry, to beg, even get mad and punch him, call him an asshole.

Just… something.

Anything rather than the plastic mask he’s been wearing ever since he decided that he wanted to be a hero. The same mask he shows everyone else.

“Let’s not jump to something so drastic, can we talk about this?”

“I don’t think there’s anything to talk about.” Mydei can be stubbornly final once he’s made up his mind, and he’s had a lot of time to think. “You can go on and be the school’s hero, and I won’t get in your way or hold you back.”

That’s when his face falls. Phainon’s upper lip is quivering, and for a moment he looks so…so scared that Mydei almost takes his words back right here, right there.

But he remains resolute.

“There’s no point in being a hero if you’re not there with me.” Phainon says so softly that he has to strain his ears to listen. “Why…” Phainon starts, and then shakes his head. He obviously knew why, and didn’t care to hear it again. “What can I do to win you back?”

Mydei just sighs, what’s the point of trying to take back something that had already happened? “You didn’t do anything wrong. I just don’t think we’re compatible as we are now….” Then, because Phainon isn’t the only one who’s been hurt, he adds in a low tone.

“Why did you have to change?”

Phainon’s jaw tightens, he’d obviously hit a sore spot. His eyes darken and Mydei wonders if he finally got the reaction he was searching for.

“I see now,” Phainon mutters, low, dangerous. “Everyone’s adoration is conditional as long as I fit the image they wanted. I didn’t realize that you were the same.”

“I…” Mydei stops, growls a little from frustration. “You’re twisting my words-”

“No.” Phainon snaps. “Have you ever considered that maybe I like the way I am now? That it’s called self-improvement for a reason. And besides, I did it for you.”

“You keep saying that.” Mydei’s voice rises as he grows frustrated, his restraint breaking. “But you never asked once about how I feel. So if you’re

doing it for your own self-satisfaction, at least be honest about that.”

Phainon doesn’t speak, he looks like Mydei had just slapped him in the face.

There is nothing but silence between them now. They are both standing next to each other, yet the distance seems impossibly far.

“Let’s just call this a mutual breakup, then.” Phainon says bitterly. He stares up at Mydei, jaw clenches, face set, as though challenging him to deny it.

“Okay.” Mydei is tired, he doesn’t want to fight anymore. “I’m moving back to Castrum Kremnos, next week.”

“What?” Phaionn raises his head again, his voice cracking. “You’re leaving Okhema?”

Mydei shrugs. “Yes.” He hadn’t gotten a chance to tell Phainon about it, but the negotiations over the summer didn’t go well. Mydei had initially planned to stay in Okhema while his parents sorted things out back home, but since his relationship is in shambles anyway, he might as well tag along. He’d be heartbroken either way, but he’d rather have family support than not.

Phainon just laughs, broken chuckles making his shoulders rack up and down. The lines are blurred to the point where Mydei doesn’t know whether he’s laughing or crying. “So you already decided everything from the start. You… you selfish bastard.”

Mydei won’t admit that he’s secretly relieved. If Phainon had gotten on his knees crying, begging, pleading him not to go, Mydei might have broken his composure. Despite everything, he still loves Phainon. But anger? He can deal with anger.

“So you can understand how I feel after all.” Is all he says, the final nail in the coffin.

He leaves Phainon there, alone, broken, and doesn’t look back. He doesn’t want to see the look on Phainon’s face if he does turn around.

Mydei’s final week at Okhema drags on, it’s horrible trying to avoid Phainon when they study in the same classroom, and he’s sure it’s the same for the white-haired boy. For the most part, Phainon seems unaffected, wearing his plastic smile like an absolute pro. Or maybe he just hides it better. Mydei has noticed him staring once or twice, when he thinks Mydei isn’t looking.

While clearing out his locker for the last time, Mydei finds the sun shaped pin he originally wanted to give Phainon after the summer break. Things have spiraled so quickly that he had forgotten all about it. Well, it’s not like he wants to keep it, but he can’t just give it to Phainon after they broke up.

Mydei should throw it away.

And yet he thinks about all the time he spent painstakingly picking out which shapes would best suit Phainon, which metals he should use, how to bend the rays just as he wanted them. It had taken so much effort… what a waste.

With a sigh, he tosses it back into his old locker, leaving it there. Maybe the janitor can throw it away, or another student will end up finding it and pawning it or something. Whatever, he just doesn’t care anymore.

Phainon is no longer his to care about, anyway.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Did You Have to Let It Linger?
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

“He dyed his hair back to white,” Mydei points out, the alcohol loosening his usual inhibition, in addition to being with trusted friends. Phainon’s hair sits longer, fluffier on the top, messy bangs framing his face. Way better than the sharp and angular blond cut he was sporting in his previous fashion spread.

Mydei hated the blond on him, it made him look so cold and so… so… foreign. “He looks better in white.”

“Oh no, we’re not doing this today. Not on the day we get signed.” Cipher says, downing her entire drink in one gulp and motioning to the waiter for a refill. “Let’s talk about literally anything else. WORK! I wanna hear about all those documents for Ms Topaz.”

Chapter Notes

These are my confessions: I love songfic I know a lot of people think it's cringe but I LOVE IT!

I hope you're all ready for yearnatron and homotron 3000... There are some POV swaps in this chapter, the reason is because when I get stuck I swap to Phainon's POV and let him wax poetic about Mydei for thousands of words.

As usual here is my twitter

The ink on their brand new recording contract was barely dry when Cipher insisted they had to celebrate at the fanciest, most expensive bar in town.

When Mydei pointed out their advanced payment wouldn’t come in until the next payday, she simply winked at him and said.

“And that’s why all the expenses for tonight’s celebration will be covered by our resident rich boy, isn’t that right, little prince?”

And Mydei sighs and gives in because why the fuck not?

It feels surreal. All the time they spent trying to build their brand by playing in dingy underground bars, in student lounges where half the crowd was there for the free pizza, in back-alley clubs where the entire audience were drunk out of their minds, recording themselves with a shitty phone camera and posting it online in hopes that they’d hit it big. And finally, it all paid off.

They made it.

Him, Castorice, Cipher, and their band Titans of Calamity had been signed by a recording studio.

Not just any recording studio, by the IPC. One of the biggest, most prestigious companies in the music industry.

“A toast, to selling our souls to capitalism!” Cipher declares, lifting her cocktail into the air and tapping the glass with manicured fingernails. She had, naturally, ordered the most expensive, extravagant, luxurious drink on the menu. Aptly named Fairy Tears, it was a layered violet monstrosity of artisanal syrups and top-shelf liquor, decorated with edible gold foil and looked like someone had dunked an entire bowl of glitter into it.

“Look at this! See how the foil is cut into the shape of tiny flowers?” She tilts the glass to show Castorice, liquid sloshing around messily inside, “Now THIS is what I call fancy!”

Castorice hiccups loudly, already half drunk from the sweet drink in her hand that probably contained enough alcohol to down a dragon. “I’m just… I still feel like I’m going to wake up in my tiny dorm room at college, and think that this is all a dream…”

“Well then get ready to pinch yourself, Princess Homebody. Because this is real, and we worked hard for this, and we’re officially rockstars now!”

Cipher raises her glass to her lips, downing her drink in one fell swoop. “Another drink!”

“Slow down,” Mydei grumbles. “You’re going to break my wallet.”

“Hey! After those all nighters we spent in the garage writing lyrics and practicing until our ears bled and I got sores on my fingers, we deserve this!” Cipher insists. “Just ask for a top up from mommy and daddy when you run out.”

“Hmph.” Mydei says. He knows his parents have his back, but ever since he opted out of being a part of the family business, he doesn’t want to ask them for money unless there is no other choice. That’s why he finds himself living a humble life these days, a tiny apartment that he shares with Cipher and Castorice, working part-time jobs to make ends meet while trying to get their music careers to take off.

And to be honest, Mydei had never felt so free. For the first time in his life, he was comfortable in his own skin.

“Fine, whatever. Cheers to us.” Mydei raises his own glass in the air, a sickly sweet pink concoction containing pomegranate juice and some alcohol that wasn’t too bitter. “To Titans of Calamity. We made it.”

“That’s what I’m talking about! Let’s go crazy!” Cipher declares loudly, causing heads to turn in their direction.

They stood out in this otherwise classy bar, and it was hard not to feel out of place. Just three misfits in a rock band trying too hard to be fancy. Their styles clashed with each other dramatically—nobody could ever agree on anything in the group chat—but at least each person committed to the bit.

Castorice, the bassist, showed up in a dress that looked like it was made by her fairy godmother. It was pink and wispy with chiffon sleeves and tiny gemstones embroidered on the skirt. Passionate at handicrafts, she had thrifted the dress and sewn the gemstones individually by hand. It complemented her long lavender hair, which was tied into a single elaborate braid flowing down her back.

Cipher, their drummer, refused to take off the cat ear hoodie that Mydei swears she’s been wearing for as long as he knew her. But at least she made some effort to dress up with her sleek black leather skirt and thigh high boots. Chunky earrings and mismatched bracelets completed the look, and around her throat sat a choker far too elegant and expensive looking for someone who claimed she was always broke. Cipher had insisted it was a gift, and Mydei was frankly too afraid to ask for further details.

As for Mydei himself, his fashion sense had matured from when he was younger. He still favoured dark colors and leather and studs and punk styled clothes, but tonight he wore a fitted black button-up, gold embroidery tracing the sides of his collar and curling down the front. His sleeves were rolled up to the elbows, revealing his muscular forearms and the swirling red tattoos wrapped around them. The moment he turned 18, he wasted no time in getting all the body ink his heart desired, and never looked back. The look was complete with straight black slacks, shiny boots, and his shoulder length hair tied in a ponytail behind his neck. He knew when to be classy when the time called for it.

As the initial clamour dwindles to a peaceful buzz—with Cipher and Castorice deep in conversation about how they’ll spend their future rockstar money—Mydei tries to relax in his seat. This luxurious atmosphere, the velvet chairs, the soft jazz band performing in the corner, loud enough to drown out the background noise, not loud enough to disrupt conversations, is unusual to him.

Maybe one day, this will be the kind of place they’re used to frequenting.

He huffs to himself, shakes his head. Nah, no matter how wealthy he gets, this kind of scene isn’t for him.

Instead, Mydei tries to picture how their lives will change after this recording deal. No more part time jobs wedged in between classes, no more nights spent in rental practice rooms. Music would no longer be something they had to cram in with their other commitments, it’ll be their lives, their full time jobs.

Instead of dingy nightclubs where the mics didn’t even work sometimes, they’ll be playing at small music festivals with an actual stage. Perhaps even with their own stage crews and sound techs. They wouldn’t have to rig their own lights and sound systems anymore.

And maybe even some day… their band name on billboards, sold out rock stadium arenas with legions of fans screaming along to their songs.

Well, maybe not now, they still had a long way to go. But a guy could dream, couldn’t he?

Castorice appeared hypnotized, taking pictures from several different angles of the sparkling cocktail that was her newest drink.

“This is just meh,” Cipher sighs, on her second drink now. “I gotta say, I still prefer the cheap apple cider over at Dolos.”

“You know that’s just apple juice and beer, don’t you?” Mydei huffs. Meanwhile, the fruity pomegranate cocktail he’s holding in his hand is quite perfect. Sweet with only the barest hint of alcohol, just the way he likes it.

Cipher shrugs. “If it works, it works.”

“Pft…” Mydei finds himself smiling, even though he grumbles, he’s having a good time. He had been worried at first, moving away from his hometown Castrum Kremnos to return to Okhema, a place that held… not so good memories for him, to pursue his dream of becoming a musician. But it worked out. He’s got a cat he adores, a few close friends who mean the world to him, and a record label contract.

Things are looking good.

“By the way, Cipher, about the documents we need to email Miss Topaz…” He says, suddenly remembering.

“Oh come on!” Cipher groans loudly, running a hand down her face. “Must we talk about work stuff now?”

“I just thought to mention before I forget…”

“Mydei, I’m drunk, I’ll definitely forget anything you say tonight anyway.” Cipher says, which isn’t true. She unfortunately, is a heavyweight with the memory of an elephant, but only conveniently remembers things that would benefit her.

Mydei sighs. “Fine, fine. I guess that shit can wait until tomorrow.”

He settles down, feeling the numbing buzz of alcohol in his head even though he’s only had that one cocktail. Despite his appearance, Mydei is a little bit of a lightweight, a vulnerability he’d rather not divulge unless it’s to his closest friends.

Mydei is content like this, listening to his friends joke over how many private jets they’ll own once they’re famous, Cipher’s sharp cackles and Castorice’s light giggles. He hears the door to the entrance open, and lifts his eyes almost lazily, not necessarily interested in whoever comes through.

Until he catches sight of a head of fluffy snowy white hair, laughing and talking to his companions. The person is tall, and his demeanor and appearance naturally draws attention, so he stands out among his friends.

Mydei hadn’t expected to see him here tonight.

Phainon.

His breath hitches as he temporarily forgets how to breathe, it feels like he’s been punched in the gut, seeing him.

He averts his eyes when Phainon looks his way, not at all mentally or emotionally prepared to deal with that piercing blue gaze right now. How many years has it been since they broke up? Four? Five?? Their lives are so different now, it would be a wonder if he even remembered Mydei.

“Little lion?” Cipher asks, noticing his weird behaviour. Her voice startles him, causing him to uncharacteristically jolt.

“Mydei, is something wrong? You look pale.” Castorice, bless her soul, has her eyebrows knitted in worry over him.

“I…” Mydei starts, at a loss for words. He better double check to make sure that it’s really Phainon before he drops that bombshell on his friends. He twists his head around to look at the newcomers, now settling by the bar counter.

It’s no use, he’s only buying time for himself. He’d known that face anywhere, those eyes, that smile. A thousand years could pass and he’d still recognize him from his stupid ahoge alone. He’d burned the memory of Phainon into his soul, and couldn’t wipe it off even if he tried.

And he has tried.

“No, no.” Cipher is saying as she follows his gaze, dread in her tone. “Please don’t tell me that guy’s your type.”

He dyed his hair back to white. Mydei finds himself thinking, as Phainon throws his head back, laughing, and his bangs fall into his eyes.

“Worse.” He says glumly. “That’s my ex boyfriend.”

Cipher’s reaction is just a tad over the top. She chokes on her drink, spluttering unflatteringly as she stares at Mydei like he’s grown a second head. “And when were you going to tell me, your dearest friend Cifera…” She starts slowly.

“...that your ex is Phainon fucking Khaslana?”

Mydei blinks at her, utterly lost. “You know him?”

“Who’s that?” Castorice chimes in, a more normal reaction from a reasonable human being. “Is he famous?”

Cipher raises a hand to her temples. “I suppose it falls to me to explain things to Princess Homebody again. Phainon’s a model, yeah he’s really famous, he’s got like—-what, several hundred thousand followers on Stellargram?”

“Oh, I see. Sorry for not knowing these things…” Castorice mumbles into her drink, blushing slightly from embarrassment.

“Don’t worry about it, It’s a compliment, babygirl.” Cipher reassures her, placing an arm around her shoulder, making Castorice giggle. “One of us has to be the normal one in the room because it’s definitely not Mydei right now.”

“Oh okay, yay.”

Meanwhile Mydei twirls his drink in his glass, he has been doing nothing but staring at Phainon for the past maybe two or three minutes now. He knows he’s coming across a little weird, maybe even creepy. But the bar is dark, and Phainon hasn’t looked his way at all, so he probably didn’t even notice him.

The thought stings a little bit.

“I thought he was supposed to walk Edo Star fashion week… What's he doing here?” He murmurs.

She was welcomed here, truly. He loved her, and rekindling their friendship even after so much time apart was easy.

But-

The problem is that Cyrene is perceptive, a little too perceptive. If he’s not careful with it, she might see through his intentions for coming here tonight.

All these worries could have been avoided if Phainon came alone. He had considered it, briefly, he didn’t want to miss his window of opportunity. But he tried to gather some company anyway because he preferred being surrounded by people.

His thoughts got too loud when he was by himself, reminding him of what he’s lost, of what he could no longer get back. Whispering the names of everything he traded away for the life he had now, and asking him if it was worth it. Questioning if he was truly happy, telling him that all this praise, this prestige, this success he has accomplished was because of luck. That he was nothing but an imposter dressed in finery and people were going to wake up and realize at any moment now that he was nothing.

But when lively and noisy people like March and Caelus were around, it was easier to pretend to be himself, to keep the voices locked away in the back of his mind. Of course, those were not the only reasons he valued their friendship, but it was an important one nonetheless.

Mydei and his friends are already inside when Phainon arrives, clinking glasses and toasting to each other. Phainon spots him immediately even before he enters, through the window, and has to avert his eyes to avoid losing his sanity. He thought he had prepared for this, but nothing even came close to seeing the real thing.

Phainon can’t even meet his eyes, it was like looking at an angel, a sight that would blind him if he stared at it too long.

Mydei is… god.

Mydei is even more beautiful than he remembers, all the pictures and grainy recordings through a phone screen didn’t do him justice. He thought he’d kept up with every new change, each new tattoo he inked onto his body, the sharpening of his facial features as the last of the baby fat melted away, the way his body only got more sculpted over time due to his relentless training.

And his face, Phainon would go to war for that face, he’d conquer entire cities if it would make Mydei smile. The way that his stern expression would soften and his gaze would almost be tender as he looks at his friends. This tenderness used to belong to Phainon alone, used to.

Now it was freely shared with other people not called Phainon. People who probably didn’t understand what a privilege it is to see that smile.

And all Phainon can do is watch from a distance and pretend not to see it.

But on the inside, he is so jealous he could die.

He knows he deserves to suffer 10 times over, he was the one to bring ruin upon their relationship. Mydei had never asked for anything, but Phainon in his arrogance had presumed to know what was the best for them. In the end, he lost the only thing that ever mattered to him.

His lingering feelings for Mydei are a part of him, as deeply ingrained as the laws of physics. He would never be able to move on, even if all he can do is hover around his traces like a fallen star.

“Phainon… are you okay?” Cyrene’s brows are furrowed, concern flitting across her pretty face. She darts her head towards Mydei’s direction and it is just as he feared, she’s caught on to something.

And he had tried so hard not to stare too, but it’s inevitable that he does because… have you seen how gorgeous he is?

“Of course, I’m fine, Cyrene. Just a little tired.” Phainon forces himself to turn his entire body away, smiling at his friend.

She doesn’t look convinced, but nods her head in understanding regardless. “You’ve been working really hard lately, don’t push yourself.”

That is when he makes the mistake of looking back at Mydei, and he really shouldn’t have.

Because how is he supposed to be normal after seeing that?

Mydei’s staring at him, looking like he jumped straight out of a ‘sexiest men in Amphoreus’ magazine spread. His head is tilted over the back of the chair, the red tips of his short blond hair framing his face, and Phainon can’t stop staring at the bob of his throat, at the red tattoos that sneak up his neck.

Mydei’s golden eyes are intense, almost glowing as they stare at him. At that moment, he looked like he wanted to devour Phainon, and he would gladly offer himself on a silver platter if it meant he would look at Phainon like that again.

Phainon’s hands are sweaty as he clutches his shot glass so hard it could almost shatter in his palm. His heartbeat resonates so loudly in his ears that it’s hard to focus on anything else.

Cyrene is looking between them like she’s figuring out a secret that only she knows.

“You know,” She leans closer conspiratorally, a hand over her mouth. Phainon instinctively copies her gesture. “That guy sitting over there is really sexy.”

Phainon freezes. Cyrene is one of his closest friends, and he knows she’s no threat to himself or Mydei. Regardless, it didn’t stop his hackles from rising, a possessive, dark, ugly predatorial instinct that screams nobody

should be looking at Mydei in the context of ‘sexy’ other than him. Because Mydei is his, even though he isn’t.

Not yet, at least.

Instead, Phainon shoves his misgivings down his throat, laughing in what he hopes is a natural and carefree way as he chokes out. “Oh, you think so?”

Cyrene nods vigorously. “Yeah, he reminds me of that person you had as your phone wallpaper.”

She’s joking, he knows Cyrene’s teasing when he hears it. But Phainon jolts anyway, panic trickling down his spine. It had been poor judgement to set Mydei’s picture as his wallpaper, knowing how easily it would be for other people to catch a glimpse of his screen, accidentally or otherwise. But he hadn’t accounted for the sheer mortification when Cyrene did actually see it and questioned him on it, and he had to lie and say it was a celebrity he admired.

Because as far as any of his current friends are concerned, Phainon is perpetually single, with a distaste for romance due to various disastrous relationships in school and college. He explained that it was better for his career that way, and they ate it up without question. Because how would he even begin to explain that he was still obsessed with his high school boyfriend to this very day?

No, it was easier for everybody to think he was just another cocky model who was only looking for casual flings and nothing more. And sure, sometimes his pathetic side slips out whenever someone reminds him too much of Mydei, but he could always chalk that up to being drunk.

“He keeps looking this way, maybe he’s into you.” She whispers. “Or… maybe he’s into me.”

Phainon’s smile is stiff as he tries to think of something to say. She’s only joking… she’s only joking… Cyrene wouldn’t take Mydei away from him. She wouldn’t fucking dare--

She laughs, tapping him lightly on the chest to pull him back into reality. “Don’t need to look at me with such a scary expression. I’m only joking.”

“...Of course, hahaha.” Phainon laughs in a way that sounds fake even to him. He glances back to Mydei, to find that he’s returned to his conversation. But his friend, the cat girl, keeps glaring at Phainon, almost like she’s suspicious of him.

“By the way,” Cyrene says, “I didn’t know you wore glasses. You look good, Phainon.”

Phainon smiles tightly. “Thanks.” They were a deliberate fashion choice. He had hoped if he looked a little bit like how he used to, if he kept some of his youthful charm… Mydei would realize that he hadn’t changed that much, not where it truly matters.

Of course Cyrene noticed.

He’s being too obvious.

Phainon tries to tone it down a little, keeping his attention on himself and his friends. He makes an active effort to ignore Mydei because if he looks back and meets his gaze well… Phainon might just lose himself completely.

It’s like handing a starving dog fresh prey, it cannot be trusted to reasonably control its instinct in the face of overwhelming hunger. Even if it’s been leashed, even if it has been domesticated, it just wouldn’t be able to control itself.

There is nothing he wants more than to bend Mydei over the table and admire his ass in those tight black slacks before fucking him senseless. Many of his fantasies have included taking Mydei home and chaining him to his bed so he would never leave again. Phainon would take good care of him, obviously, treat him like a king, give him everything he desired, make sure he knew he was loved each and every day of his life. He would make Mydei happy, be the perfect, doting husband he deserved.

Still, he forces himself to be a good boy, to be patient. He’ll have to take things slow, reacclimatize Mydei to his presence. He can’t act too rashly, doesn’t want to spook him.

But all his best laid plans go flying out the window when Mydei suddenly takes to the stage with a guitar.

“Wha— huh?” Phainon mouths, head jerking to attention. He knew Mydei had decided to pursue music as a career, it was why he came back to Okhema, but he never had the privilege of listening to him sing live. Going somewhere so crowded is asking for trouble, and would most certainly blow the cover he had tried so hard to maintain.

Besides… hearing that voice again, the one that used to sing only to him, being broadcasted in front of a live audience was just too overwhelming. At least in recordings, the voice was filtered first. Sound waves converted into electric current, stored as ones and zeroes before being relayed to the listener. A digital wall keeping them apart.

But make no mistake, Phainon is his biggest fan. He’s watched all their videos, looped them over and over so many times it must seem obsessive. His favourite ones were the short song covers Mydei posted on his personal account, the ones where it was just his voice, his guitar, and the camera zoomed in to his glorious pecs—the guitar, he means. And he owns more than a few pieces of merch, from t-shirts, to a signed poster from their first ever gig, and some strange finds like an old guitar pick Mydei had apparently used and threw away. If only so it would stay out of the hands of those less deserving.

And now… he is really going to hear Mydei sing in person.

Phainon didn’t know if he had been blessed or cursed by the gods.

Mydei begins to play, and Phainon’s breath hitches. Those notes… are so familiar to him that it hurts.

He had only heard them once, when Mydei played it for him in his room, the same day they had their first kiss. They had been two stupid teenagers

then, and everything was simpler.

Like all things, the memory faded with time to the point where Phainon couldn’t recall the melody or the lyrics. But it was always in the back of his mind, some shattered remains of a tune he thought he would never hear again. Phainon had grieved, assuming that it was lost to him forever.

But hearing these opening notes makes all the memories return, and resurfaces the feelings that never went away.

Mydei’s singing voice is deeper than he remembered. Older, more mature, definitely sexier. Every word sends chills down his spine.

And I’m in so deep You know I’m such a fool for you You got my wrapped around your finger Did you have to let it linger?

Does he know what he does to Phainon, when he’s singing so beautifully while looking at him like that? Phainon can feel the heat of his gaze, his golden eyes practically boring into him, stripping him bare.

Phainon hasn’t had that much to drink at all this evening but he already feels drunk. He’s drunk off yearning and longing and from the way Mydei’s husky voice wraps around his heart in chokehold.

Does he know that Phainon still yearns for him? And is it even possible to hope that Mydei feels the same way?

No, no, Phainon must not allow himself to be delusional.

It’s enough that he was able to hear that song again. He does not dare ask for more, doesn’t want to overstep the line. This time, he’ll keep that memory close to his heart, even if he can only admire from afar.

But Phainon desperately wanted to leap over that gap.

Chapter End Notes
