chapters.title: Chapter 4: Don't Blame Me, Blame My Ex
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Mydei forcibly drags his eyes away. It’s one thing to ogle the man when he thinks he’s not looking, it’s another to do it right in front of his face. “It has. I see you’re doing well.”

“You can say that,” Phainon smiles at him, though it seems a little hollow. “Could be better.” His eyes are fixed on Mydei, like he’s the only person in the room. It’s intense but also… a little bit exciting. Their knees knock underneath the table, and Mydei pulls his legs back, breaking contact. He doesn’t want to indulge him too much, not until he knows what Phainon’s real intentions are.

“What do you mean, better?” Mydei echoes.

Mydei feels Phainon’s ankle hook around his leg again, possessive, dominating. At the same time, he leans forward on the table, putting himself in Mydei’s personal space.

“Better if I didn’t see you flirting with another guy the second I walked out of the room.” Phainon says in a low voice, his tone bitter. “I can’t leave you alone for even a minute, can I?”

Chapter Notes

Me knowing full well that I'm bad at writing fight scenes: but what about I do it ~anyway~ This chapter is a long one! Phew, over 12k words, lock in.

Additional content warnings: Male Original Character (don't mind him his only purpose is to move the plot along), Stalking

Mydei doesn’t think he’ll ever get tired of applause.

Adrenaline rushes through his veins when he hears the audience clap and cheer after he performs, filling him with a buzz that is like nothing else. There is no better feeling than knowing his work had been recognized, enjoyed, savoured, even. With the stage lights shining into his face and his ears ringing from the guitar reverb, the world is narrowed to only himself, and Phainon who keeps staring at him with lights in his stupid blue eyes.

Emboldened, he smirks into the mic. He’s got a few choice words for the stupid, beautiful HKS sitting over there.

“You like that? The next song is called ‘fuck you, you motherfucker, suck my-” And the speed at which Cipher darts up on stage and drags him away before he can get them all kicked out can only be described as superhuman.

“Thanks everyone for the love, but he’ll be leaving now.” She says cheerfully, adept at damage control.

“Geez, he’s not even a rockstar yet and he’s already causing trouble.” Cipher sighs as they arrive back at their table, Castorice shoving a glass of ice water in his face. “You’re never impulsive like this, Mydei. Seeing your ex must have gotten you really worked up.”

“Maybe we should go home.” Castorice suggests. “It’s pretty late and we’ve been here for a while now…”

“No… I’m fine. I’m over him.” Mydei insists, though they don’t know if he’s lying to convince them or to convince himself. Regardless, he’s fooling no one.

“I can’t believe I’m agreeing with Princess Homebody on this, but I also think we should go home.” Cipher says. It’s clear that Mydei isn’t in the right headspace after seeing Phainon, and continuously being in the same room can’t be good for either of them.

“No.” Mydei says, firmly, stubbornly. He does practically everything but dig his heels petulantly into the ground. “We’re staying until I say we can go home.”

“Ughhhh…” Cipher places a palm over her face, dragging it downwards. When the little prince says he doesn’t want to do something, nothing will change his mind. It’s both his most admirable, and his most annoying quality. “Have it your way, you brat. But I’m cutting you off.”

And that’s how Mydei ends up sipping only water and fruit juice. His eyes stray over to Phainon again, whose friends, red-faced, some of them swaying and barely upright, are getting up to leave. Mydei knew he wasn’t mistaken, he had been staring at him like there was nothing else in the room. Surely, that song had sparked something within him, a forgotten feeling, a realization that he missed him, anything.

But if that was true, then how can he just sit there and talk to his friends like nothing’s happened while Mydei is sitting here in shambles? Perhaps he was wrong, and it was only his imagination and wishful thinking. Mydei had no choice but to curse himself, this is why he doesn’t bother with blind optimism.

He watches quietly as Phainon stands up with his arm around the beautiful pink-haired woman. He’s going to leave too, so it’s really coming to an end, just like that.

Phainon doesn’t spare Mydei a single glance as he escorts his drunk friends out of the bar, nodding to the bartender on his way out.

How cruel.

Maybe Mydei really is the only one clinging to the past, chasing a shadow that had never belonged to him. It’s clear that the Phainon of today is somebody who is warm, kind, talented, beautiful, the kind of person that everybody wants a piece of. Hell, a person who gives a piece of himself freely to everybody.

His heart aches with something that feels like grief, which is weird because the person he’s mourning is very much alive. But Mydei forces himself not to dwell on it, he’s wasted too much time grieving a relationship that has been dead and buried for a long time.

It would be great if he could drown out his feelings with even more drinks, but since Cipher has cut him off, that’s probably for the best. With his returning sobriety, he realized he had caused trouble for his friends tonight.

“What is taking Cassie so long? I only asked her to get us a few non-alcoholic drinks.” Cipher grumbles, looking over her shoulder.

Right, it had been a few minutes since Phainon and his friends left, and seeing how dejected he is, Castorice volunteered herself to get them some refills. Mydei hadn’t even noticed her kind gesture, he truly is the worst.

He raises his eyes to the counter, and meets Cipher’s gaze only for her to grin conspiratorily at him. A tall and handsome stranger is standing there, talking to Castorice. While she is usually an introvert who gets shy when talking to new people, she’s conversing with him amicably, looking very invested in their conversation.

“Tonight is full of surprises,” Cipher says. “Cassie getting along with someone aside from us… they grow up so quickly!”

Mydei squints at the scene in disbelief. The stranger is tall, broad-shouldered, dressed in an oversized black sweater and ripped black jeans. He can’t get a good look at his face because his back is facing them but…

He certainly seems her type. “I thought Cas preferred women?” He asks aloud.

“She does, but she likes both.” Cipher says. “Look at her speaking so confidently and passionately! I wonder what they’re talking about?”

They didn’t have to wonder for long, as a few moments later Castorice nearly skips up to their table, bringing the stranger with her.

“Hello,” She greets, a little too cheerful for the occasion. “This is Nicola. He’s the drummer of the band that was playing earlier and we went to the same alma mater.”

“Hey.” The stranger, Nicola, says.

“Hi.” Cipher greets. “I’m Cipher, this is Mydei.” She nudges his side, hard, motioning him to respond.

Mydei doesn’t even try to hide his sigh as he responds with the air of someone who’s being greatly inconvenienced. “Yo.”

He knows he’s being a brat and feels slightly guilty for it. It’s just that… he’s having a tough night, and he was kind of hoping it’ll just be the three of them instead of having to put up with a stranger.

Cipher nudges him again in the ribs even harder this time, making him flinch.

“Mydei, sure you don’t have something to say to the drummer of the band you interrupted earlier?” She says with gritted teeth.

“I apologize for disrupting your set earlier,” he says reluctantly. It feels weird, it’s usually him making Cipher apologize for the trouble she’s caused, oh, how the turntables.

“No, it’s alright. It was refreshing, actually.” The guy gestures to the empty chair at the table, and Castorice nods, giving him permission to sit. “It’s been a while since I’ve been that entertained.”

Okay, so this was happening after all. They were getting a fourth ranger, that’s fantastic. Mydei sighs, allowing Castorice and Cipher to carry the bulk of the conversation. He’d never been a particularly sociable person to begin with, so this is the norm for them.

But even though he doesn’t contribute to it, he’s still very much a part of the conversation. That’s how he learns that Nicola is a junior from Castorice’s alma mater, who did music as his major.

“Isn’t that amazing?” Castorice says, sparkles in her eyes as she directs her attention to Mydei. “You two must have so much in common. You have a degree in music too, don’t you Mydei?”

“I guess?” Mydei just says bluntly, furrowing his eyebrows. Why is she being so persistent and almost… hopeful? Surely, she does not seek Mydei’s approval that badly. He has no qualms about who she’s dating as long as the other person isn’t an asshole.

“Oh…” He feels almost bad at the way Castorice seems to wilt slightly at his nonchalant reply before turning her attention back to the stranger. “Do you have any hobbies, Nicola?”

“Boxing,” he replies confidently, and Mydei won’t lie, that kind of piques his interest.

“What a coincidence!” Castorice says. “Mydei is very passionate about mixed martial arts.”

“Huh.” Mydei says, finally taking notice of the man called Nicola for the first time. The guy’s obviously well-built underneath his loose jumper, so he’s probably not lying about the boxing thing. When he raises his hand to scratch at his nose, Mydei can see tattoos covering the back of his hand, extending to his wrists and possibly the rest of his arm as well. His face is, he supposes, objectively handsome. Sharp features with a multitude of facial piercings that seems to add to his good looks rather than detract from them. His jet black hair is messily cut, uneven layers framing his face, and his eyes are a piercing shade of bright red.

His gruff, badboy demeanor is the opposite of clean cut Phainon, Mydei thinks unhelpfully to himself.

“She’s right, I enjoy doing martial arts.” Mydei tells him. “I find that it helps with stamina and coordination, alongside a robust diet and exercise plan.” If anyone knows his kryptonite, it’s Castorice. He can discuss fitness for hours.

“I feel the same, I still lift regularly, but boxing improves my footwork and mobility.” Nicola says. “What’s your split between martial arts and functional training?” Castorice looks beside herself with delight that the conversation is finally moving somewhere.

“Martial arts two or three times a week, strength training in between, your usual push-pull-legs. One or two active recovery days a week depending on my schedule.”

“Look at that! You’re bonding!” Castorice squeals, sounding a little too excited about a conversation on fitness. Mydei never thought she’d go for a gymbro and is just about to tell her so when Castorice suddenly says-

“Cipher, I’m really craving a burger. Will you come with me to the fast food joint down the street?”

“Huh?” Cipher says, looking confused for once. “We can’t just leave Mydei here.”

“He’ll be fine!” Castorice insists, tugging her by the wrists. “He’ll have Nicola here to accompany him. Please?”

Cipher was never able to resist Castorice, especially not when she started begging. So as expected, she sighs and reaches for her bag, looking at Mydei as she stands up.

“You heard the princess. Are you okay on your own?”

“I could come with you to get the burger–” Mydei stands up, he’s feeling a little peckish himself. Normally he wouldn’t touch something as unhealthy as a burger, but it’s been quite the evening and he deserves a cheat day.

“NO!” Castorice said so abruptly Mydei can’t help but sit back down. “I mean, it’ll be rude to leave our new friend hanging. You guys should totally… continue your riveting conversation! Goodbye!”

“Call us if anything happens, Mydei!” Cipher says, in lieu of a goodbye.

Castorice grabs Cipher’s hand and they leave together while he looks at them like someone who’s been betrayed. Because that person is him, he’s being betrayed.

He may be a little slow on the uptake, but he’s not completely oblivious. It’s obvious to him now that Nicola is here not because Castorice likes him, but

because she’s trying to set Mydei up with him.

Her efforts are appreciated, he knows the girls worry about him, but they’re ultimately misguided. He’s in no state to get to know someone, not when Phainon is still so heavy on his mind.

Mydei is just thinking of how he could politely excuse himself from the conversation when a waiter places a vibrant yellow cocktail in front of him.

“It’s a Pina Colada,” Nicola says. “My treat. Castorice told me you preferred sweet things.”

Mydei clicks his tongue in annoyance, his sweet tooth was supposed to remain a secret within his friend group. Why is she going around telling his weakness to random strangers? But… he hated wasting a perfectly good drink. Not finding any good reason to refuse, Mydei mumbles his thanks and takes a sip, exhaling deeply at the burn as the sweet alcohol rolls down his parched throat like nectar.

If the circumstances were different, Nicola is… fine. He’s easy on the eyes, friendly, and Mydei could tell that they have some hobbies in common. But… his eye colour is all wrong, his hair colour isn’t white, he isn’t teasing Mydei in the exact way he wants to be teased, his smile doesn’t send his heart into overdrive. He just… he’s not Phainon.

It would be unfair to lead on a perfectly nice guy when his heart obviously lies elsewhere. Maybe one day, when he fully gets over Phainon, he’ll consider dating again. He doesn’t know when that day will be.

“I apologize. I’m not looking for a relationship right now.” Mydei says, making up his mind. “Not looking for anything casual, either.”

“Oh.” Nicola says, eyes widening to the point where he looks like a surprised animal. “I wasn’t… oh… okay.”

The table descends into an awkward silence.

“I’m sorry if I gave off that impression.” Nicola apologizes sheepishly. “I’m… not too good at making friends.”

“Oh.” Mydei replies, since that is truly all he can say. Guilt stabs him like a knife and Mydei feels heat rush to his neck from shame. How could he be so conceited to assume that a random guy would be interested in him in that way? How could he have shot him down so coldly and heartlessly without even an ounce of saving face? “I apologize for misunderstanding.” It was the least he could do, but it still didn’t seem like enough.

“Oh, no, no!” To make matters worse, they now seem to be looped in an endless cycle of uncomfortable apologies. “It’s my fault for coming on too strong. I met a fellow gym junkie and got too excited…”

Mydei’s facial expression twists, here was a guy just trying to be friendly, bonding over similar hobbies, and he just assumed that he wanted to get into his pants. He of all people should know how it feels like to have your intentions misunderstood just for being awkward, and here he is doing the same to someone else.

Regret for his careless actions seemed too mild a term. He is mortified, he wants to sink six feet down underground and never return. If Nikador would throw down a lightning bolt onto the very place where he sits and vaporize him on the spot, Mydei wouldn’t complain.

“It’s fine… really, I’m not offended. I’d still like to be friends, if you’re open to the idea.” Friends? Friends?? Mydei can’t even look the man in the eye. “Are you okay though? You don’t look well.”

Mydei doesn’t feel well.

“I—uhm—I’m just going to go to the bathroom,” He says, standing up so quickly it makes his head spin.

“Oh, okay… I’ll be here.” No, Mydei pleads silently to nobody in particular. Please leave, he wouldn’t be offended.

As he walks towards the direction of the restroom, Mydei feels the back of his neck prickle. It’s an uncomfortable, uneasy feeling, like he’s being watched, scrutinized. Mydei turns around, looking behind him. Nothing is amiss. Nicola has his back turned to him, nobody is looking at him.

Trying to ignore his agitation, Mydei takes out his phone and idly unlocks it, hoping for a distraction, any distraction.

He’s not comforted one bit by the messages on his phone. Castorice and Cipher had sent messages to their Titans of Calamity group chat, messages that read along the lines of ‘Go get him little lion!👍’ ‘Remember to stay

safe and use protection!’ ‘Text us if you’re not coming home tonight’

Oh… they misunderstood the situation so badly. Was he really so pathetic that they felt the need to set him up like this?

He needs to get a hold of himself.

The bathroom is thankfully, unoccupied. Mydei admits he spends longer than what’s socially acceptable inside, just splashing cold water on his face in an effort to sober up. Droplets trickle down his chin and drip into his collar, but the chill is welcomed, it wakes him up and brings him back to his senses.

For everything that’s happened tonight he blames the alcohol. Clearly his faculties weren’t all intact, and he solemnly swears not to touch a drop of drink again.

Just then, his phone buzzes with a private message from Cipher.

Cipher: Hey little prince, hope you’re not too mad that we ditched you earlier. Cassie wouldn’t have done it if she wasn’t sure you were in good hands, so don’t worry! It’s just… none of us want to see you sad like that. Just try… please? For Cassie’s sake.

Mydei sighs and pockets his phone. He knows they meant well, but it doesn’t feel good, having the choice taken out of his hands.

He glances at his reflection in the mirror to check his face and hair, noting that he looks a mess, cheeks flushed and ponytail lopsided. The bathroom window is reflected in it as well, showing nothing but the dark and deserted sidewalk outside. And while he’s staring at it, something moves outside, so imperceptible Mydei wouldn’t even have noticed if he hadn’t been looking.

Mydei pauses, narrowing his eyes, a chill is running down his spine. It could have been anything, a shadow of a pedestrian, a stray cat passing by, a cloud briefly blocking out the moon, but it makes the uneasiness grow.

He has no proof, nothing but a paranoid, unsettling feeling.

Mydei shuts his eyes, steeling himself with a deep breath. He’s going to go out there, apologize to Nicola again, grab his jacket and leave. Then, he’s going to call a cab, go home, take a shower, and then sleep it off. Tomorrow, everything will be back to normal, and this will be some awkward memory he’ll laugh about with Cipher and Castorice.

“You look unwell,” Phainon gently brushes his knuckles against Mydei’s temple, slick with sweat. He winces in pain as it brushes across a graze. Well, he’s not feeling his best, he did just get his ass handed to him in a shameful display.

“I just want to go home and rest,” Mydei murmurs. Phainon steps into his personal space far too comfortably despite the years they’ve spent apart. He slips his arm around Mydei’s shoulders to support him like he weighs nothing, and eases him down on a nearby bench to rest.

“Let me call a cab to take you home.” Phainon offers, taking a seat next to him. He’s still close, so close that Mydei can feel his body heat. Phainon’s arm curls around Mydei as he pulls him closer to his chest, holding him possessively, almost lovingly.

“This… this is unnecessary.” Mydei protests, trying to push himself away to no avail as Phainon’s arm only tightens around him. He’s too drained to put up any sort of fight.

Phainon just laughs, not the sneering, condescending laugh from before, but something cheerful, light, like all his burdens had been lifted. “Then just think of it like you’re doing me a favour. You’ll allow me this much, right? For old times sake.”

His fingers slide into Mydei’s hair, undoing his tangled ponytail and gently threading through the soft golden strands. Mydei has to hold back a pleased hum from the back of his throat from how nice it feels. Despite the chilly weather his hand is warm, the way he strokes Mydei’s hair is so gentle, and the slow rise and fall of his chest as he breathes is nice, relaxing.

“Let me take care of you, please.” Phainon murmurs, and it works like a charm, with Mydei’s eyes fluttering closed as a wave of exhaustion overtakes him.

Mydei doesn’t know how things have come to this, with Phainon cuddling him like he’s a doting boyfriend rather than an estranged ex. But Mydei would be lying if he said this wasn’t something he had been dreaming of for a long time. To be held in Phainon’s arms again, for Phainon to pamper

him, whisper sweet words in his ear, to treat Mydei like he was the most important person in the world, the only person that matters.

It’s more than he can wish for.

There is still a lot that Mydei doesn’t understand, and he doesn’t know how long this strange, possessive, loving version of Phainon will even last. But would it be so bad if he took advantage of this? Just for a little while.

“Just close your eyes and get some rest,” Mydei’s brow furrows slightly as he feels fingers gently push his bangs aside, and a soft kiss, light as butterfly wings, lands on the center of his forehead. “Our cab will arrive soon.”

…

‘Our’ cab?

Mydei frowns a little bit at the phrase, but the feeling of Phainon running his fingers through his hair is just too relaxing, and Mydei starts to feel the knot in his chest unravel. He missed this, he missed being close to Phainon so much that it hurts. He’d assumed their breakup was permanent, that he’d never get to be held in Phainon’s arms like this again. Just this tonight already seemed too good to be true, like he’d wake up hungover tomorrow and realize that it was all just a dream.

He sighs lightly, feeling Phainon pull him impossibly closer as his steady heartbeat thumps softly underneath his sweater. Mydei listens to the rhythmic beating, letting himself drift off a little bit as he practically melts against Phainon.

“You look so beautiful like this, Mydei, all cuddled up next to me.” Phainon murmurs, running his fingers down his braid, tucking the ends of his red-tipped hair behind his ears. “You’re going to make me greedy, you know.”

Mydei’s relaxed expression doesn’t move, his breathing deep and even indicating he’s fallen asleep. Phainon doesn’t even know if he can hear him.

The events that come after are a drunken blur to Mydei, partially passed out from exhaustion on Phainon’s shoulder. He remembers Phainon gently walking him into a cab, giving him sweet encouragement as he does so. He remembers Phainon’s arm around his waist, warm, protective, affectionate throughout the entire car ride. He remembers hearing Phainon’s voice as he made small talk with the cab driver.

“Oh, we’re alright. He just walked into a lamp pole and took me down with him, he’s a bit of a lightweight!”

Mydei had a bone to pick with that, he would never get hurt in such a stupid way like walking into a lamp pole. He got that injury in battle, against a worthy opponent, like Kremnoan traditions dictated. But what comes out of his mouth instead is a pathetic, half-asleep grumble.

“Haha, I guess he didn’t like me calling him a lightweight.”

“He’s lucky he’s got a nice young man like you looking out for him.”

“Of course, he’s the most important person to me.” With the way Phainon’s arm tightens around his waist as he says that, Mydei could almost believe that he means it.

Mydei wakes with a start when the cab jerks to a stop. The sudden inertia causes him to lurch forward, and then backwards again. He grits his teeth, preparing himself for the impact of hitting the seat, only to feel Phainon’s palm cushioning the back of his head.

“Mydei, we’re here. Can you walk?” Phainon asks, in a voice so sweet and gentle that Mydei had to look around to check that he was referring to him.

Mydei nods, his body is fighting to go back to sleep, but he insists on walking out of the cab on his own, stubborn to a fault. It occurs to him, as he steps outside the car, that he had never told Phainon his address. But Phainon had spoken as though he knew exactly where to take him.

This doesn’t look like the apartment he shares with Castorice and Cipher, no, this high rise condominium is much too extravagant for anything they

can afford.

Behind him, he hears the remnants of a conversation between Phainon and the cab driver.

“Young man, if you don’t mind me asking, are you that model—”

“Mister,” Phainon interrupts, tone strained. “Here’s a tip as thanks. And… I would appreciate it if you would keep tonight between us.”

The cab driver pauses. “Well,” he says, “It’s not my business to pry into young people’s private matters.” Followed by the screech of tires as the taxi drives away.

“Where are we?” Mydei turns around, mouth thinned out into a grim line. He knows the answer already, but wants to hear it confirmed from Phainon’s own mouth.

“I did say I was taking you home,” Phainon says, expression a little sheepish as though he knows what he’s done. “My home, I meant.”

Mydei’s frown deepens, he’s feeling better, more sober, more like himself after the brief nap in the car. He’s now clear headed enough to realize the implications of Phainon bringing him here.

“I can’t do this,” he says bitterly.

Phainon blinks at him, all wide eyed innocence. “What are you talking about?”

Mydei rubs the bridge of his nose, does Phainon really take him for a fool? Well, he’s done himself no favours, considering he’s been acting like one all evening.

“Is this how you get all those one-night-stands? You sweet talk them and get all handsy until they come home with you? You're gonna try that on me too, huh?”

Phainon gapes, mouth opening and closing like a fish out of water. It’s almost funny to see if Mydei’s heart wasn’t breaking all over again.

“If all you’re offering is sex, then I don’t want it.” The back of his eyelids are stinging, and Mydei feels himself tearing up. It makes his injured eye burn even more. “I’m not someone you can just fuck and abandon.”

Mydei closes his eyes for a beat longer than necessary, hoping it comes across as exasperation and not like he’s upset or anything.

Because why would he be upset? They’re nothing to each other currently, and everything Phainon was doing could be attributed to seeking closure or even tying up loose ends. He knows, he knows.

“What the fuck?” Phainon splutters, finding his tongue. His swearing catches Mydei off guard and he blinks in surprise, not expecting such foul language from Okhema’s golden boy. “No! That was never my intention. I wanted to take you home to look after you while you sober out! You were never going to be a one-night-stand.”

Mydei’s vision blurs over, the world turning hazy before his eyes. He had not cried since the breakup, not even a single tear, today will not be the day he breaks that streak. Even though he never wanted to be a one-night-stand, it still hurts like hell to hear Phainon reject it. Because of course, what kind of insane person would consider bringing their ex home for sex? It certainly seems crazy to him.

“Then thanks for your offer, but I’ll be fine.” Mydei tells him, feeling his emotions stabilize as the hope in him flickers and dies. “I’ll just call Cipher and wait here until she picks me up. I don’t need your sympathy or your generosity.”

Speaking of which, he hadn’t even managed to check his phone since the last time. He wonders if Castorice and Cipher are going crazy with worry, bombarding his phone with texts and calls. He’s a bit annoyed at them, but he never meant to stress them out.

“Mydei,” Phainon places an arm on his shoulder, which Mydei shrugs off. He can’t believe he let Phainon touch him so freely before, he must really be out of his mind. “You’re in no condition to be alone.”

Mydei glares at him, feeling the first drop of rain fall on the top of his head, cold and annoying at the same time. “I won’t be alone,” he says stubbornly. “I have my friends to look after me.”

“And where are they now?” Phainon asks him flatly. “Your friends ditched you in the bar with a stranger, Mydei.”

Mydei blinks, the raindrops are coming faster now, getting into his eyes and into his shirt. “Quit pissing me off. Nobody ever died from being lonely, or else I’d have died a thousand times already.

Phainon’s breath hitches, and he recoils as though he’s been hit. His eyes are shiny as he looks at Mydei, something wet trails out of the corner of his eye as he blinks. Mydei tells himself it’s only rainwater, because the alternative makes his heart ache.

“...you were lonely?” Phainon asks him softly.

Mydei swallows, feeling like he’s revealed too much. It must seem awfully spoiled and contrite of him to declare himself lonely, especially when he’s got two loving parents who are still alive, relatives who dote on him and a healthy friendship circle in both Castrum Kremnos and Okhema.

But leaving Phainon had felt like ripping out a piece of himself, a hole that he never managed to patch up. To have and to lose him was worse than never having him at all. It taught him that no matter how close you were to someone, it was only temporary.

Everything could change in an instant.

“I didn’t know what loneliness was until you changed, and I couldn’t even recognize you anymore.”

Phainon’s expression twists, his fringe is flattened on his forehead from the rain, water rolling down his cheeks, and his eyes are red as he raises his voice and yells. “I changed because I thought that I could help you!” His voice cracks. “Then I became so caught up with everyone’s approval, into becoming the kind of person I thought everyone would want, until I didn’t even know who I was anymore.”

Mydei frowns, completely speechless. He just cannot understand his way of thinking at all. Throughout his life, Mydei had grown up around people who encouraged and supported his self-expression; he had always been at odds with the rest of the world but… it never seemed to matter. Even when he entered adulthood, he met like-minded souls like Castorice and Cipher who seemed to swim against the current.

But just because he didn’t understand doesn’t mean he didn’t want to understand. Listening to Phainon was something he should have done years ago, but he had been too young and stupid to, convinced that cutting off the relationship was the best thing to do.

“I devoted myself into becoming a perfect person that would make you proud, someone who could please everyone.” He laughs bitterly. “Then I lost you, and it just seemed… so meaningless. The sacrifices were utterly pointless if I couldn’t even keep the person most important to me. I didn’t know what else to do, so I just… kept on pretending. At some point I stopped thinking about what I really wanted, or what kind of person I really am.”

His admission only makes Mydei feel sad, empty. He doesn’t understand why Phainon would put himself through that. The chasm of their different ideologies stretches before them, uncrossable.

“I just don’t understand why you thought that was something I’d want,” Mydei grits out. He can’t help but be honest, even if it hurts, even if the pained whimper that comes out of Phainon’s mouth stabs him like a knife. “You knew what my principles were, what kind of person I am.”

“Of course you wouldn’t understand,” Phainon laughs, brittle and bitter. “You were already effortlessly cool without even trying. What would you

ever know about changing yourself to be wanted? I didn’t have the self-assuredness that you had, the security net you had. I didn’t have the privilege of moving to a whole different country if I failed!”

There were no blows exchanged this time, but Mydei flinches like he’s been hit nonetheless. He knows he was lucky, he knows he was born privileged, and he has no doubt his upbringing had shaped him as a person.

“This is why we went our separate ways.” Mydei only says softly. “You and I didn’t see eye to eye, we still don’t.”

“Mm, I guess not.” Phainon agrees, his expression is subdued, his eyes are dimmed. He looks like Mydei had sucked every ounce of joy and whimsy out of him.

It’s a horrible, painful sight to see, and if anything, it only makes Mydei more certain that his decision to walk away was the right one. He hated that he was the one who made Phainon look like that.

“I’m sorry-” Mydei says.

He’s a hypocrite, he knows. Mydei is stuck in a cycle of tormenting himself and doesn’t know how to get out of it. How many times now had he told himself that he was going to move on from Phainon? That he was going to unfollow all of his social media pages and delete his accounts. That he was going to focus on his studies, his career, or his music. That obsessing over his ex is pathetic.

Mydei had always been good at restraining himself for the greater good. There are things he wants that are not good to have. Milk and cheese in his pomegranate juice, honeycakes drowned in strawberry syrup, and Phainon.

~*~

Phainon’s heart sinks when he sees Mydei make that face.

It features prominently in his nightmares.

All these years and he still makes the same fucking expression. Eyebrows tightly furrowed, jaw set, mouth in a straight line, a determination in his golden eyes that indicates that he’s already made up his mind.

And Phainon is 17 again, standing in a stifling park at the tail-end of autumn. Just the two of them standing side by side, but feeling like they’re miles away. Phainon was so stupid then, so naive, not understanding how the subsequent events would change his life forever. And Mydei, with that same self-righteous expression on his face because he thinks he’s doing the right thing.

History repeats itself, and if Phainon doesn’t do something to stop him now, Mydei is going to leave him again.

Thorns are crawling up his throat, there’s blood in his mouth. His chest feels too tight, his ribcage clenching around a heart that is battering at its restraints. Adrenaline floods his body, telling him that he’s going to die if he doesn’t move, doesn’t do something to stop this from happening!

He’s gone through it before, the hollowness of knowing that someone he loved was out of his reach. Years of surviving from scraps, looking from afar, getting updates through stalking and social media. Not being able to do anything but watch as Mydei moves on with his life, spends time with other people, smiles at someone else.

The idea that Mydei will one day find love with someone who isn’t Phainon makes bile rush up his throat.

And the worst part about it all was that he still had hopes for tonight. Still thought that if he could just get Mydei to stop and listen, if he was honest for once and tore himself open to show Mydei how he felt, that they could still have a chance.

He failed.

He ripped his raw, red, beating heart out of his chest and offered it up on a silver platter and Mydei still didn’t want it.

Something in him breaks.

Phainon has tried being nice, he’s tried being vulnerable, he’s tried appealing to reason. He really was trying to do things the easy way, but Mydei’s actions had left him with no other choice.

It’s Mydei’s fault for being so stubborn.

So be it, if Mydei tries to shut him out, he’ll kick the door down, hell, he’ll smash it to pieces if he needs to. If Mydei tries to walk away from him, Phainon will track him down and bring him back. Even death would not be able to separate them, because Phainon will follow him to the underworld and back.

If Mydei still doubts his resolve, then so be it.

“Sorry-” Mydei is saying to him. Phainon can almost read his lips as he opens them to utter ‘We shouldn’t see each other again’.

“No need to apologize.” Phainon says, bitterness seeping in every word. “When you’re not sorry.”

When he sees Mydei tilt his head in confusion, it means he’s taken the bait.

“You’re doing it again, you know,” Phainon continues. “Jumping to conclusions, making the decision all by yourself. Bold of you to lecture me when you haven’t changed a bit, making the same mistake as you did in our youth. You’re not even going to give this a chance?”

Mydei stills, and Phainon can practically see the gears in his head turning as he thinks it over “Say I humour you, that I throw the dog a bone,” Mydei says with a sneer. “What’s your suggestion then?”

Phainon points at the sky, which is pouring. “First, we get out of the rain. You come to my place to dry off, we’ll both get some much needed rest. No strings attached.”

Mydei eyes him warily.

“What? You don’t think I’ll actually be able to do anything without your consent.” Phainon raises his hands, putting on a reassuring smile.

“Relax. There’s security cameras all over the building. The door will be unlocked, you can leave at any time. And you still have your phone. I may have won our fight earlier, but we both know I can’t overpower you in strength.” Please, if he could, he wouldn’t need to bother with mind games.

Besides, it doesn’t take a master of observation to tell that Mydei is irritated and uncomfortable. His clothes are soaked, sticking closely to his body. He’s shivering slightly from the cold, even though he’s trying valiantly to hide it, and the bruises from their earlier fight must be painful.

Phainon’s apartment is spacious, comfortable, warm, and he can see Mydei actually contemplating the suggestion.

He’s on the hook, now Phainon just has to reel him in.

“And after that, if you still want to leave and go home. I won’t stop you. In fact, I’ll respect your wishes and leave you alone. Forever.” Phainon says.

He doesn’t want to do that, he doesn’t want that at all. He’s a determinator at heart, the kind of guy who would move mountains to get what he wants. But right now, he has no choice but to tell Mydei what he wants to hear.

Mydei is stubborn, but he is also painfully naive in the way where he thinks everybody is as honest as he is. Mydei lives in a world where promises are kept, and never broken. It appears nothing has changed in that regard.

He can see Mydei’s eyelashes quivering as he comes to a decision.

“I have your word?” He asks.

Phainon nods, hand on his heart. “I promise.” He says.

With that, Mydei seems to relax. He slumps forward slightly, letting down his guard enough for Phainon to see just how exhausted he is. “Then… fine,

just for a little while.”

Victory had never tasted so bitter.

Phainon feels guilt clawing at his throat for taking advantage of Mydei’s trust in him. But it’s not like he’s lying, Phainon fully intends to keep his word.

If Mydei still wants to leave later.

Phainon’s brought himself time to show him why they’re perfect for each other.

He heaves a deep, shuddering exhale, the cold wind chilling him to the bone. He’s won the battle, for now. However dirty it is, however unseemly, a victory is still a victory.

“Let’s go,” he says.

When he was a student at university, Phainon had a professor that many called insane. This valued teacher had taught him that the methods did not matter, as long as he obtained results. Sure, there were many among the faculty who greatly disliked Professor Anaxagoras for his…almost sacrilegious ways, but he had some good points. Sometimes, playing a little dirty is necessary to achieve one’s goal.

Mydei looks a little uncomfortable entering Phainon’s swanky, upscale, modern condominium building. When his wet shoes squelch and leave muddy footprints upon the freshly mopped marble floors he hunches over so deeply into his jacket that he looks like he wants to disappear in it.

But Phainon doesn’t care, he pays his cleaning fees like everyone else. Instead, he just beams and waves cheerfully at the doorman as they walk in so that he does not pay Mydei too much scrutiny as they head deeper towards the elevators.

“Don’t look at him,” he leans close and whispers into Mydei’s ear, feeling a slight shiver as he does so. “Just look at me.”

“You’re too close,” Mydei complains. When he turns his head, a wet strand of hair brushes against Phainon’s cheek, so distracting it’s driving him mad.

“I already told you I’d stay, you don’t need to be so clingy.”

Reluctantly, Phainon takes a single step back like it’s the hardest thing in the world. Casual as anything, he keeps two of his fingers in Mydei’s belt loops like a lifeline, just because he wants to touch him somewhere to know he’s still there.

He can feel Mydei’s skin, warm underneath the fabric and almost shivers at how close they are.

If Mydei didn’t like it, he’d push him away, say something.

Mydei’s silence is consent.

The wait for the elevators is excruciating. Now that Phainon’s standing so close to him, he can faintly smell the floral perfume that Mydei’s using. It’s barely there, but it’s still intoxicating. Hungry for more, Phainon subtly moves his face closer to the back of his neck, slowly inhaling the mixture of fading perfume, rainwater, and the man’s natural scent.

He commits everything to memory, the feel of Mydei’s warm skin, his smell, the way his chest heaves as he inhales in and out. He never wants to forget this moment.

The elevator dings, and Phainon guides Mydei gently inside, barely registering pushing the button for his floor before the doors close with a light click. That is when Phainon lets go of his grip, giving Mydei space.

As much ‘space’ as is allowed anyway in this cramped elevator. Even if they both stood on the opposite ends of the elevator that would still be… really close. Phainon feels it in him, the instinct to pounce on Mydei, to pull him closer… even closer to the point where he can’t run away.

He wants to do that so badly, but he had promised Mydei, no ulterior motives, just to shower, sober up, and rest.

Mydei leans against the wall as the elevator begins its ascent, rocking slightly against the movement. He doesn’t say a single word, just lifting his gaze to look at Phainon with an expression he can’t read.

The wall he’s leaning against is a mirror, and Phainon doesn’t even recognize the person reflected in it. Somewhere in the back of his mind, he knows it’s himself, caught at his most primal, at his worst. His eyes are darkened and bloodshot, pupils dilated until there is nothing left but a thin blue ring around the edges; his carefully styled hair is in complete disarray; and his expression looks insane.

It’s perhaps the most honest reflection of himself in a long time. Is this the version Mydei is seeing now? He’s selfish though, so selfish that even if this side of him disgusts Mydei, he doesn’t care.

Phainon tears his eyes away from that hateful person in the mirror. He doesn’t need to look at that, not when a god is standing before him.

Mydei’s jaw tightens, he’s clenching his teeth so hard Phainon can see the tendons on his neck protruding. He turns away, expression impossible to read as always. But not before Phainon gets a glimpse of it, the look in his eyes that makes his throat go dry and heat rush to his abdomen. It was so brief, but he’d seen it for sure, a look in his golden eyes that is a reflection of the same darkness and desire in Phainon’s own. .

“Mydeimos…” He whispers, carefully brushing his tattooed cheek with the softest touch. “Look at me, please.”

When Mydei refuses to turn around, Phainon takes hold of his chin a little roughly, turning his face towards him.

Yeah, it’s unmistakable, as much as Mydei tried to hide it. The undeniable lust and hunger reflected in those beautiful eyes.

Phainon had assumed it was rejection, but what if it was restraint instead?

What if… Mydei wanted this as much as him?

It’s dangerous to be too delusional, but Phainon feels himself falling and he’s unable to stop.

He feels his entire body shaking as he swallows. “Haha, what’s with that face? You look like I’m about to jump you.”

He hears Mydei’s breath hitch, a tinge of pink staining his cheeks before he turns away again. He can’t make eye contact when he's embarrassed, just one of the qualities he finds so cute in Mydei.

“Do what you want.” He mutters.

A dangerous offer to put on the table. Mydei has no idea just how badly Phainon has yearned for this. He has no idea that Phainon has jacked off to him for years, religiously, faithfully. How everyone he tries to take to the bedroom needs to have a combination of blonde hair, tattoos, or a muscular

body that can rival the gods. Nothing and nobody else comes close to making him hard. Even then, his cock turns flaccid so quickly when his brain finally catches up to his body and he realizes that no matter how he pretends otherwise, they’re not Mydei, and they could never be Mydei.

Mydei has no idea how his fantasies have only gotten more perverted and obscene from years of being pent up. How many times he has thrusted his cock into his lonely fist as he watches a video of Mydei singing on his phone, how many times he’s touched himself to pictures of him taken off the street like a fucking creep.

He really can’t. If Mydei gives him an inch, he’ll take a mile. Before he knows it, he won’t be able to stop himself. The beast, once released, can’t be put back into the cage. He’ll eat him up, he’ll leave no scraps.

This… this will have to do.

Phainon leans closer, enough for Mydei to feel the warmth of his exhale, to see the sweat beading on his temples even though the weather is cold. Their scents mingle in the narrow space between them. Mydei with his soft florals, a complete contrast to his appearance; Phainon with his clean and woody perfume, the one he had promoted once and got so many compliments on he just… kept wearing it ever since.

“Don’t tease me.” Phainon murmurs, low and shaky. He doesn’t say more, he can’t. He shoves his hands in the pockets of his coat, they’re damp and cold and kind of disgusting but he squeezes the fabric with his fists. It’s the only way he can stop himself from touching the beautiful man in front of him.

The jut of his red tattoos stand out starkly against his sunkissed skin, the lines running brash and bold, the flame-like design creeping up his neck.

Phainon imagines his tongue tracing along the lines of those tattoos. They hadn’t been there when he was a teenager, but it looked so natural on him that Phainon could almost assume that he’d been born with those tattoos, that they were a part of his skin. He had said so before, that he thought Mydei would look good with them. Good is an understatement, he’s fucking irresistable.

He closes his eyes and tries to channel all the people in the world who do not want to jump Mydei as soon as they’re alone together. How does everyone else do it? It seems totally impossible.

He’s breathing so heavily, it’s embarrassing. He probably sounds like a perverted freak, but he can’t help that it feels so stuffy in this elevator. He tugs at the neck of his turtleneck, lowkey regretting that he chose this outfit even though it makes his body look amazing. It feels like he’s suffocating in here. Nobody is speaking, so all he can hear is his own breathing. Maybe his friends were right when they called him a dog, he’d be a dog for Mydei, he’d get down on all fours and bark if that was what he wanted.

The black collared shirt is soaked with rainwater, sticking tightly to the curvature of his muscles. Mydei’s pecs move along to the rhythm of his breathing, in… and out…

In… and out…

Seeing them so close at the bar, Mydei admitted he got a little jealous. Cyrene is gorgeous, the kind of feminine beauty that makes heads turn when she walks down the street. Long, silky pink hair, an expressive face

with delicate facial features, a walk so graceful it almost looks like she’s dancing. Phainon could have her, if he wanted. He couldn’t imagine anyone saying no to him.

So why settle for Mydei even after so many years?

It boggles his mind.

As he flips through the pages, he realizes this magazine is from the future. Flicking to the front cover again, he notices that the date printed on it is a few days from now. This is probably an advanced copy sent to Phainon since he’s got an interview feature in it.

The Phainon fan pages that he still follows would go into a frenzy if they knew he got his hands on such a treasure.

He could leak it…

…or not.

Shaking his head, Mydei perishes the thought. It may be a little selfish, but he wants to keep this find to himself; the fans won’t die from waiting a couple of days. One of the perks of having a personal relationship with Phainon.

He starts reading the feature.

The shirt? Supima Cotton. The man? Boyfriend Material. Phainon Khaslana reflects on his views on relationships, career, and whatever comes in between.

It’s all contrite, polished fluff, but Mydei finds himself combing it from line to line anyway. Anything that could give him an edge on understanding the man Phainon had become would be welcomed.

But he finds nothing.

The version of Phainon interviewed is refreshing as a spring breeze, the nation’s perfect boyfriend. A kind and handsome gentleman whose tastes are… bland at best. His favourite colour is white, his favourite drink is water, his favourite animal is the dog, his favourite season is winter. It’s almost offensive in its inoffensiveness, like he’s a caricature designed to appeal to everyone.

Up until yesterday, reading this article would have bothered him immensely.

But tonight he’s seen Phainon’s B-side, the side that picked a fight with Mydei so they would both feel better. Who is so obviously, deeply into him that it’s flattering and embarrassing. Phainon who is needy and pathetic and a bit of a loser yet is all the more endearing for it.

Mydei is still combing the article when Phainon finishes his bath, walking into the living room while running a towel through his hair.

He freezes when he sees Mydei sitting shirtless on the floor, wearing nothing but borrowed sweat pants and leafing through a magazine with Phainon’s face on it.

Mydei looks up, seeing Phainon staring at him, mouth agape, as though his brain had decided to shut down for the day. He’s frequently shirtless at home, and the girls think nothing of it except that he’s gross. He’d forgotten how it felt like to be looked at with such thinly veiled lust.

Not that Phainon hadn’t been looking at him that way all evening, ever since their eyes met in that bar. It was just easier to ignore when there were other obstacles in the way, other baggage they hadn’t worked out.

Now though, there’s really no excuses or distractions.

“I…I see you still haven’t put on the shirt.” Phainon mutters, eyes fluttering away. “I chose it because it was black, and that’s your colour. You don’t like it?”

“I don’t. That shirt should be set on fire,” Mydei says flatly. “I refuse to wear it.”

Phainon’s lower lip juts out in a pout, utterly unfitting for someone whose face is plastered on the cover of magazines. He changed into loungewear too, and the pathetic aura is amplified by the white t-shirt he’s wearing, printed with a graphic of two chimeras cuddling alongside a caption so lame it doesn’t even bear acknowledging. The purple track pants do nothing to redeem the look, and his hair looks like an uncombed bird’s nest.

He doesn’t look anything like the picture perfect hottie in the photograph, quite the opposite. And Mydei must be down bad, down horrendous even, because if he had to choose, he’d pick this version of Phainon any day.

“I didn’t know those kinds of magazines would interest you.” Phainon tilts his head towards the magazine in his hand. “I thought you’d prefer like.. Nature or something.”

Mydei shrugs, he does enjoy subjects like nature and history a little more, but he’ll read pretty much anything he can get his hands on. Knowledge is powerful, regardless of the topic. “It was a very interesting article.”

“You’re making fun of me,” Phainon scowls. “Stop.” He eyes the magazine like it had personally insulted him. “I tried to talk them out of it, but they really insisted on going with the ‘boyfriend’ angle.”

“I’m not making fun of you,” Mydei says. “I thought the writer was being very sincere.” He says, accidentally giving away the fact that he had read the feature cover to cover. “You have qualities that many would consider desirable in a partner.”

Instead of cheering him up, Mydei’s reassurance seems to have done the opposite, as Phainon’s shoulders droop, making him look even more like a soggy wet dog. “A lot of people, but not you, right? I have money, I have fame, I have looks. I can be the perfect man, the ideal boyfriend.”

His voice cracks, and it suddenly becomes apparent to Mydei that this has been a source of their insecurities for a long time.

“But it’s still not enough for you. Because no matter what I become, how high I go, it’s never going to make you want me.”

Mydei closes his eyes, exhales out slowly. He’s not the short-tempered youth he used to be, time and maturity had mellowed him out. He wonders if Phainon had somehow missed all the signs, or whether he deluded himself into thinking that the feelings weren’t reciprocated.

“HKS.” Mydei curses. “Who says I don’t want you?”

Phainon blinks at him in confusion “I mean I assumed-”

Mydei rolls his eyes “And of course you assumed incorrectly.”

He grabs Phainon’s cheeks and squeezes them in his hand, it makes his lips purse like a pufferfish. He looks stupid and lost and totally adorable as he looks at Mydei with confusion. “Listen to me, because I’ll only say this once.”

“You have always been enough for me, exactly as you are. I never wanted more from you. My only wish was for us to remain the same forever. I couldn’t understand why you needed to capture the hearts of others when you already had mine.”

Mydei flushes and releases his grip on Phainon, breaking eye contact. He may be honest, but he’s also a guarded man who’d rather keep his thoughts to himself, or skirt around the issue especially when it’s something personal to him. Airing his heart out like this made him feel vulnerable, but he supposed if anyone deserved the truth, it was Phainon.

This man who had apparently waited for him for years, even though there was no guarantee they’d ever cross paths, much less get back together. The man who haunts his thoughts more often than not, that Mydei inevitably compared every new potential partner to. The man whose red string of fate he could never break, no matter how far they drifted away.

Maybe one of his hopes when he moved back to Okhema was the idea that he would meet Phainon again someday.

Phainon exhales, long and deep “You know,” he murmurs, resting his head on his knee “I’m trying so hard to be a good boy tonight. You’re making things… difficult.”

The way his voice drops in timbre sends jolts of excitement down Mydei’s spine, he feels like he’s toying with someone who's on the verge of snapping.

“How,” Mydei teases, resting his chin in his palm. “Am I making things difficult?”

Phainon tilts his head to regard him, now that the turtleneck is gone Mydei can clearly see the golden lines on his neck, tattooed in the likeness of a sun. The shape is familiar, but Mydei can’t put his finger on why…

“You pleasured yourself in the bathroom without me.” Phainon says, counting off his fingers. “You almost kissed me in the elevator, and now, you’re sitting here, practically naked, showing off that absurd body of yours, in my living room.”

“It’s like you don’t even know what you’re doing to me.”

Mydei smirks, and then he drops the magazine on Phainon’s lap to cover the signs of his obvious arousal. Raising his arms over his head, Mydei stretches, slow, relaxed, like a cat. His back arches, shoulders pushed backwards, chest up and out. As he feels his abs clench, he knows the way it makes his tight muscles stand out.

“So?” He replies, belligerent.

Phainon gapes at him, at a loss for words. Then he turns away, face the same colour as an apple, discreetly wiping his sleeve across his mouth.

“I can’t.” Phainon murmurs, burying his head in the crook of his elbow, face burning. “You told me in no uncertain terms that you didn’t want sex.”

“Then you spectacularly misinterpreted my intentions,” Mydei corrects. “I said if all you’re offering is sex, I don’t want it.”

Phainon’s voice is muffled as he’s still hiding in his elbow, but Mydei can vaguely hear the words as he sulks “Yes I heard you very well the first time.”

“If you’re offering something more, though.”

Phainon turns his head a little bit, just so that one blue eye peeks out underneath his curtain of hair. The quivering of his pupil almost… hopeful as he says in a tiny, meek voice. “More? Like what?”

“Hmm, I dunno.” Mydei thinks he’s spoken enough, left hints that even the most clueless would pick up. “That onus is on the one offering.”

Phainon gulps, licks his dry lips, and looks down at the floor.

“So.” Mydei continues. “What do you want, Phainon Khaslana?”

Chapter End Notes

chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

“I love you.” He blurts out, not able to stop all his emotions from leaking out.

“Stupid.” Mydei’s words are harsh, but his voice is so unbearably gentle. His face looks like he’s trying hard to hold back a smile.

“Say it back.” Phainon says, tugging at Mydei’s clothes, voice soft and weak like a child. Because he’s insecure, because he needs the reassurance, because even if he somehow manages to fuck things up again at the very least he can record that soundbite to loop in his mind for all eternity.

Without saying a single word, Mydei leans forward and kisses him.

Chapter Notes

I have been accused of edging my readers last chapter. These accusations are all true and I regret to say that the edgings will continue. /The crowd boos, tomatoes are thrown at me, Phainon and Mydei are having gay sex in the back row.

Some additional CWs: Female OC (don't worry about it she is just there to move the plot along), dry humping, oral, stalking

Back in high school, when Phainon was the student council president, his vice-president had once asked him what he would like to receive as a present.

“What?” Phainon had said, caught off guard. They were sitting across from each other, two opposite sides of the table. As usual, Phainon’s side is

stacked with paperwork, student proposals, flyers that needed to be distributed and displayed and checklists that needed to be vetted. Their school’s open day was in less than 2 weeks, which meant that things were really hectic. Phainon barely has time to eat, much less think about things like this.

“Yeah, a gift,” his vice-president said cryptically. Her name was Arielle, a straight A student, captain of the basketball club, the kind of girl that was universally adored by both teachers and students. She tilted her head to regard him, long blonde hair falling like a curtain over her shoulder. “Your birthday is soon, isn’t it?”

Phainon had no idea, he’d genuinely forgotten about it.

Birthdays at the Khaslanas were quiet, family oriented affairs. His mother would bake him a birthday cake, their family’s secret recipe, and they’d sit down for a family dinner. If they were still in Aedes Elysiae, they’d probably have invited the neighbours over for a birthday party, making things livelier.

But not in Okhema. He couldn’t expect his parents to take additional days off just because it was his birthday. He dares not ask for more, dares not seem ungrateful, since his parents had already sacrificed so much already by uprooting their lives to move here when he got his scholarship.

There was once a time where he had dreams about adding a 4th person to his birthday celebration. He’d invite Mydei over to his small, humble apartment, they’ll play dumb party games and he’d sneak him out to his favourite takeout spot down the street after his parents had gone to bed.

Mydei would whine and complain all the way there because he hated unhealthy food. But he would give in eventually, because he always let Phainon do whatever he wanted.

Now it was just… a stupid fantasy he had, nothing worth thinking too deeply about.

“A gift? For me?” Phainon deflected the subject with an easy smile. “Well, I’d like some cushions for the chairs in the student council room, they’re pretty uncomfortable. Or something like a label maker would be great! I’m always getting confused on which tray the approval forms are supposed to go in.

“I’m not asking about what the student council wants,” Arielle repeated blandly. “I’m asking you what you want.”

Now he feels put on the spot. Their conversation had drawn the attention of the other student council members working in the room, and they were now staring at him in anticipation.

It suddenly occurred to him that everyone was invested in this conversation because despite spending the entire year working closely together, none of them knew him well enough to choose a present for him.

What did he want, anyway? Phainon had no idea.

The things that came to mind he wouldn’t classify as ‘wants’. More like… deep desires that he doesn’t let himself indulge in.

He wanted Mydei back. But even Phainon knew when something was downright impossible. Mydei’s in Castrum Kremnos now, doing okay for himself from the sparse content he uploaded on social media. Besides, nobody knew they dated, and it seems weird to dig up a dead horse.

He wanted everyone to take responsibility for their own problems for once instead of pushing everything to him because he’s the student council president. That included the teachers, who frequently added to his workload because he was such a trustworthy and competent student.

He wanted people to stop looking at him like he’s some kind of messiah for just a moment. And yes, the irony wasn't lost on him, he molded himself into this image on purpose and now he wanted out? Try not to laugh.

No, no, a want should be something more tangible, something actually obtainable. Something he could hold in the palm of his hand, something

like…

“...the limited edition ‘Amphoreus Saga of Heroes’ Dawnmaker enamel pin?” He thought.

“Huh?” Arielle asked, eyes nearly boggling out of her skull.

Phainon quickly backtracked, he’d said too much, he wasn’t supposed to share that out loud. “Or dogs? I love dogs! Any dog themed item is good with me!”

Everyone likes dogs, don’t they? And Phainon is a little dog-like himself so that makes total sense. It was the safest option to pick.

He doesn’t actually expect to be given something.

When his birthday arrived, the student council members pooled their funds together to get him a coffee mug that said ‘Stay Pawsitive!’ with a silly cartoon dog on it. It was impersonal, appropriate, and so utterly basic that Phainon couldn’t help but let out a sigh of relief.

It’s for that very reason that it was perfect.

Aside from the usual well wishes, a few handwritten birthday cards and a surprise celebration thrown in the classroom during lunch, nothing out of the ordinary happens. It’s nothing he can’t handle, it’s nothing he doesn’t deserve.

The curveball came when they said their goodbyes after school and Phainon turned around to head home.

Arielle calls his name to stop him right as he’s walking out of school grounds.

“Is there something wrong?” Phainon racked his brain, he’s pretty sure he’d completed all his duties for the day. Stamped every form, filed every document.

“No! Nothing’s wrong,” Arielle shifted on the soles of her feet, uncharacteristically nervous. “I just wanted to give you something.”

Phainon started getting a bad feeling about this. “Can it wait?” He asked, trying hard to exit the situation but not in a way that would cause offense. “I’m sorry, it’s just– I’m in a hurry.”

“It will only take a second!” She pleaded, pressing her palms together like a prayer.

Her blonde hair was tied in a half-ponytail that day, glimmering in the light of the setting sun. Her hair tie had cherries on it, bobbing playfully as she moved her head. Phainon made it a note to notice these little things about people because he knows that pointing it out made them happy.

Mydei would look good with a little cherry hair tie. His hair is short but he should still be able to tie the longer locks back. He’d get so mad though, if Phainon tried it on him. Something about being too cutesy, something about making him look like a fool.

Geez, Mydei had been gone for a year and Phainon still thought about him, he’s hopeless.

“Okay, what is it?” Phainon asked, dragging himself back down to reality. Mydei’s not the one standing in front of him, Arielle is. She deserved basic respect, at least.

She wrung her hands as she continued speaking. “I just… well… you said you wanted this. You backtracked about it later, but I just thought… maybe you were just too embarrassed to say you wanted it. So here!”

She pulled it out of her pocket before offering it to him, the Dawnmaker pin he had his eye on.

Phainon stared at it for a beat longer than necessary.

Arielle continued speaking. “I looked up this game and… this is the sword the main character uses, right? The hero. It makes sense, because you’re…

you’re the hero of our school.”

“This is too expensive.” Phainon said immediately, mouth dry. “I can’t accept it.”

“No! No, it’s fine. I stumbled across an online listing. Someone was clearing out their collection, so I got it for cheap.” She was lying, because Phainon stalked the listings religiously and he knew that none of them had been sold for anywhere near ‘cheap’.

Guilt flooded his entire chest. He knew that she’d gotten it to make him happy, and he wanted to be happy. The collectible Dawnmaker pin was something he’d had his eye on for a long time.

He should have just accepted the gift with gratitude but instead, Phainon felt sick. He wished he hadn’t mentioned his stupid, selfish request at all, wished she hadn’t listened, wished she didn’t go out of her way to spend money on it.

He didn’t want to feel like he owed her something.

“Can I pay you back?” Phainon asked, panicking.

Arielle smiled, but she looked annoyed enough for Phainon to know that he’d said the wrong thing.

“That’s not the point of a gift,” she pouted. “Plus, you’re always wearing that sun pin on your blazer, so, I thought you’d like this.”

Phainon unconsciously grasped at the lapels of his jacket, feeling the pointed edges of the metal engraving dig into his palm. He hadn’t realized anyone noticed. He’d been so careful that he normally wore it on the inside of his blazer, hidden from view.

He’d found it in Mydei’s locker the day after Mydei stopped coming to school. He had just been checking it to make sure Mydei hadn’t left anything behind, there was no other reason. The craftsmanship was sublime, the metal was probably real gold, and the etchings were in a

language he couldn’t read, presumably Kremnoan. It seemed obvious that it was a gift Mydei had intended for him, and ended up never actually giving it to him because of… everything.

When Phainon realized this, he took the gift home and cried. He'd kept it on his person ever since, not able to bring himself to part with it.

“Y-you noticed?” Phainon repeated shakily.

Arielle blushed, tucking a lock of hair behind her ear. “I mean… sometimes you hang your blazer on the chair in the student council room and I just… see it.”

The thought that he was being scrutinized so closely made him uncomfortable. He preferred to be the one observing, noticing things about people. He did not like having the same done to him.

He was not dumb, nobody would pay this much attention to someone they weren’t at least a little interested in. He knew Arielle harboured a crush on him, it was obvious!

“C-can I put it on you?” Arielle gestured to the Dawnmaker pin again, face flushing pink.

Phainon nodded shakily. He supposed there was no harm and… he couldn’t really say no. Not after she went out of her way to get him such a thoughtful gift.

But when her hand reached out to him, his heart seized with panic because her hands were on the wrong pin. For some reason, she’s fumbling with the sun pin, Mydei’s pin, the last scrap of himself that he left behind before disappearing from Phainon’s life.

“That’s not yours!” He snapped, voice clipped. Before he could think about it he’s reached out to grab her wrist, stopping her from doing anymore damage.

Arielle looked up at him, green eyes wide with surprise and fear. And with a start, Phainon realized he’d let his composure slip. That wasn’t gentlemanly of him, it didn’t suit the prim, proper, gentle image he’d built for himself over the past year.

He quickly let her go, but his hand hovered over to the pin, clutching it like a lifeline. “Sorry! It’s… very important to me. Please don’t touch it!”

“I only wanted to adjust it as it was crooked.” Arielle said slowly. “I’m sorry.”

He watched her carefully, almost warily as she pinned the Dawnmaker onto his lapels, correctly this time.

“There,” she said, stepping back and surveying her handiwork. “It suits you.”

It didn’t. Dawnmaker is the sword of a hero, and Phainon was nothing but an imposter.

“I…” Phainon swallowed, feeling the pit in his stomach grow. “Thank you. It’s a wonderful gift, truly. How can I make it up to you?”

Arielle shrugged, a small smile on her face. “You don’t have to. It’s a gift. You do so much for everyone else, you deserve something nice too.”

Phainon wanted to grab her by the shoulders and shake her until she opened her eyes because he did not. He is a mess and has made so many mistakes and is fucked up in ways she cannot even imagine.

But he couldn’t say any of that, so he simply smiled. “I really want to repay you somehow, please?” He looked at her intently in the way that he knew many students found irresistible.

And she folded like wet tissue paper.

“Then… maybe we could go out for coffee sometimes?” She squeaked. “Not for student council stuff, just you and me.” She shrugged, casual as

anything, though the action was given away by how red her face was getting.

Phainon understood immediately, she was asking for a date.

The relief made his shoulders sag down, of course, everything is transactional, this was what he understood of the world. Mydei was an anomaly, somebody who threw the axis of his world off balance precisely because he never asked for anything in return.

But when he thought that Mydei was just like the rest of them, that his love was conditional as long as Phainon adhered to the image he wanted… it broke him.

Bitter with the memories, Phainon plastered a smile on his face. “Okay,” he agreed. “We can do that.”

Arielle smiled at him so brightly that Phainon told himself it was fine. Agreeing to date her hurts no one and costs him nothing. That was what he’s good at, bearing everyone’s wishes on his shoulders, making others happy. Just a blank slate for other people to project their ideal man onto.

Even something like wanting a stupid collectible keychain led to him being in a relationship he didn’t want to be in, one that dragged on for two months before she finally dumped him right before graduation.

The experience taught him that wanting always came with a price tag.

Even now, sitting here, Mydei is laying his heart at Phainon’s feet and saying it’s his if he wants it. And Phainon… still can’t say anything.

“I… I’m not sure.” Phainon murmurs, hugging his knees. He feels small and vulnerable and weak and stupid.

It’s just… he’d thought that as long as he had Mydei in his life, he’d be okay with that, no matter what unconventional, toxic form their relationship

took. Mydei was the person who understood him most in this world, and losing him again was unthinkable.

If Mydei hated him, he’d claw back into his good graces. If Mydei disappeared from his life, he’d chase him down until he finds him again.

It’s impossible to explain all this without sounding completely unhinged, and Phainon doesn’t even know where to start.

Mydei sighs, and maybe even looks disappointed? Phainon isn’t sure.

“I’m sorry if I put you on the spot. You don’t need to give me an answer right now.”

With that, he shifts away, creating distance between them.

“W-wait!” Phainon says, panicking. What if his indecisiveness has annoyed Mydei and he wants to leave, the straw that broke the camel’s back? Phainon would give him an answer now! Is ‘everything’ a valid response? He’ll take whatever Mydei is willing to give him!

“I don’t want you to rush. Take all the time you need to think about it,” Mydei says gently, like he read his mind. “Just do me a favour, and make sure that you’ll be thinking about what you want, for once.”

“Huh?” Phainon repeats dumbly.

Mydei rolls his eyes. “You heard me. When you’ve come to a decision, make sure it’s one that you’re making for yourself.”

With that, Mydei gets up. The air around Phainon feels much colder from his absence. The man makes himself comfortable on the couch, pulling on Phainon’s favourite old worn yellow hoodie for warmth—a seemingly casual action that is driving Phainon a little insane, because he had no right looking so good in it.

Mydei stretches out on the couch horizontally, relaxed and lazy, before he grabs his phone and starts scrolling through it.

“Are you going to sleep now?” Phainon asks softly.

“I don’t think I’ll be able to get much sleep tonight,” Mydei says honestly. “But thank you for allowing me shelter at your home.”

He knows Mydei is giving him an out, respecting his personal space and comfort. He’s a coward who led the lion into his trap and now doesn’t know what to do with it. He wants Mydei, that had never been in doubt. But it’s hard when Mydei’s also the cautious type, the type who puts the ball in his court, an open invitation to come and get it, if he’s brave enough.

They both can’t dance around each other forever.

He watches Mydei quietly as the latter’s phone buzzes incessantly, message after message flowing in. The blue light from the screen softens his features, and Phainon can’t help but think that he looks gorgeous like this. But as the messages keep coming, and Mydei’s beautiful face is marred by a light frown, feelings of anxiety come flooding in.

He’d overheard the conversation between Mydei and his friend, Cipher earlier. She was warning him about Phainon, something about him being a psychopath, that he was dangerous. She’s not… totally wrong, but he never meant any harm. He would admit to loitering around places where he knows Mydei has been. Sometimes it’s enough being in the same place, breathing the same oxygen. Sometimes… it’d take a little more to satisfy him. Little trinkets, or souvenirs to remember where he’d been; proof that Mydei was there.

One man’s trash is another man’s treasure, or so the saying goes.

He didn’t think anyone noticed, he’d been so careful about it.

“Who are you talking to?” He tries subtly looking over at Mydei’s phone screen. There are… definitely a lot of messages from the same person.

His worry spikes.

“If you wanted to look at my phone…” Mydei says calmly, eyes still fixed on the screen. “You could have just asked. I didn’t appreciate being locked out.”

Phainon’s blood freezes.

So he knew?

Phainon hadn’t intended to go that far. The phone was just lying there, and he couldn’t resist the call of temptation. Phainon had tried several different combinations of Mydei’s birthday, only to get irrationally upset when none of them worked. He’d felt frustrated that he didn’t even know Mydei well enough to guess his phone password, and in a fit of hubris had tried his own birthday.

That locked the phone, and sealed his fate.

“I’m sorry!” The apology spills out of him frantically, and he defaults to grovelling now that his cover has been blown. Panic floods his veins. What if this is the breaking point for Mydei? The  straw that breaks the camel’s back and makes him decide that Phainon is too… too much, too crazy, too obsessed, too unhinged. “I… I was just too curious. Please don’t get mad at me?”

“I’m not mad, I’m just–” Mydei says.

But Phainon has already spiralled, and he can’t stop. Things had been going so well, they were going SO well and he just HAD to ruin everything with his stupid impulsive decision.

He knows that rifling through somebody’s phone is a terrible offence. Unforgivable, even. Phainon would hate it if the same was done to him. He’d feel so violated, so disrespected.

“There’s no way you’re such a saint,” Phainon says.

“Not a saint. Just… don’t have any secrets, not from you.” Mydei admits quietly. “So if there’s something you wanted to know, just ask. I’ll tell

you.”

He can’t say things like that so casually, it makes him feel sick. It’s like he’s baring his weak spot and offering Phainon the blade. The amount of trust he’s put in Phainon makes him unwell, it makes him want to dig and dig and make his home in Mydei’s skin.

“What… what is your friend telling you about me?” Phainon musters the courage to ask.

Mydei purses his lips, silent, but angles the phone for him to see.

Message after message of accusations, with evidence to back it up. His friend is pretty impressive to have collected this all within a few hours. Grainy security footage of himself in disguise outside Mydei’s gig venues. Another clip, several seconds long, different venue, different disguise, but undeniably him. There’s even one of Phainon loitering in front of an apartment block, which, according to the panicked messages, is the one that Mydei is currently living in.
