“I don’t give a fuck what other people think.” Phainon interrupts sharply, words coming out almost venomously, gaze sharp and piercing. “This is what broke us apart in the first place, caring too much about what everybody else thought.”

Mydei pauses, Phainon’s hands are gripping his so tight that his knuckles are white and trembling.

“I don’t want to wait anymore. And I don’t want to make that same mistake again. So… let me ask you this time.” Phainon pleads. Mydei sighs and closes his eyes, knowing what question is coming.

“What do you want, Mydei? Do you want to be with me?”

What an unfair question to ask him. The answer is yes, the answer has always been yes. Even when he tried to bury it, even when he pretended that he had moved on, the feeling was always there, in the back of his mind. It lingers like a parasite he can never shake off.

Even the most carefully built fortress will crumble when faced with Phainon’s sincere and clear blue eyes, his expression open and vulnerable.

“Yes. I do.” Mydei surrenders, waving his white flag. “Fine. You win. But you will be in charge of explaining to my friends why we got back together so quickly.”

Phainon’s lip curls up into a smile, slowly, like he’s still in disbelief that Mydei has even accepted him. It lights up his face to the point where Mydei has to look away lest he be blinded by the radiance. His ability to suddenly transform from a cold, handsome beauty to an adorable puppy in the blink of an eye should be studied.

“That’s easy!” Phainon says cheerfully. “I could talk for hours about your incredible personality, your absurd body, your amazing ass, how sweetly you moan when-”

“Shut up! Now.” And there is no better way to shut Phainon up than by kissing him into submission.

And well, one thing leads to another, and they may have gotten a little carried away. Next thing he realized, they’re on the couch again. Mydei’s shirt is crumpled, one side of it tucked out and wrinkled. The collar is open by a few additional buttons, revealing the fresh new hickies on his neck and collarbones. His braid is messy, he will need to do his hair again.

Mydei is starting to realize that this level of physical attraction is not conducive to his daily life. He can’t keep his hands off his (no longer) ex-boyfriend, which is a very real problem. He won’t get anything done like this!

But when he sees Phainon sitting with his head tilted back against the couch, lips swollen from kissing, a matching hickey on his neck over that godforsaken choker and a smirk that could set him on fire, it makes Mydei want to throw all caution to the wind and jump his bones all over again.

That would be extremely unproductive, so Mydei mentally reminds himself to stay strong and tries to distract himself by having a better look at Phainon’s collection of video game paraphernalia. He’d been fairly interested in it since last night, but admittedly he had been… quite distracted with other matters back then.

Looking around, Phainon really is a huge ‘Amphoreus: Saga of Heroes’ fanboy. He has a collection that many fans would kill to have. In addition to the games themselves, he’s got the artbooks, limited edition foil prints,

figures, and even a poster signed by the developers. On the edge of a shelf is a corkboard, cluttered by various keychains and pins dangling off it, smaller trinkets he had collected over the years.

Mydei’s eyes catch on to one in particular. “Oh.” He remarks, plucking it out for a closer look. “The limited edition Dawnmaker enamel pin. You finally got it. You used to yammer on about wanting this non-stop.”

He remembered Phainon whining and whining about how much he wanted it and how cool it was because it reminded him of his favourite hero.

Mydei had considered getting it for him as a gift, he could certainly have afforded it. But in the end he opted for some dorky handmade pin instead. He didn’t know why he did that, in hindsight. Maybe from some innate need for it to be special, for it to be the only one of its kind.

He always figured he’d have the chance to go out and buy the Dawnmaker pin some other time.

But it looks like Phainon managed to obtain one anyway.

“Oh,” Phainon shuffles his feet, looking uncharacteristically nervous. Mydei hadn’t even asked him how he obtained it, it didn’t cross his mind. But Phainon blurts it out like he’s been carrying it as a guilty secret for some time.

“Actually… it was gifted to me by… uhm-” He seems to wrestle with himself for a second before admitting. “...one of my exes.”

“Huh?” Mydei clenches the pin in his fist.

These collectible pins, although limited edition, were still produced en-masse by a gaming company. They were made of cheap alloy, probably nothing as good quality as say—authentic Kremnoan steel. And when Mydei applies pressure on the narrower part of the sword, like so, it bends slightly under the force, feeling like it would snap.

“I’ll throw it away!” Phainon grovels. “I should have done that years ago! It just… never came to mind. I completely forgot about it! That’s how little it meant to me.” He steps closer, hands flailing like he’s not sure whether he should touch Mydei to comfort him or not.

“Mydei, don’t be mad, please?” His blue eyes are watery, voice tinged with panic.

“I’m not mad!” Mydei says calmly (or so he thought) as the pin snaps into half under his grip with a sharp ‘crack’.

They both stare at the shattered pieces of the enamel pin.

“I’m sorry,” Mydei apologizes, alarmed. He’d been annoyed, but hadn’t meant to break it. He’s not the type of guy to just destroy things he doesn’t like. He generally tries to keep himself under control so this was all terribly embarrassing.

“No, no. You just did what I was going to do.” Phainon trails off, and as he keeps looking at the broken pin his face gets progressively redder. “You just snapped metal using your bare hands. That was… kinda… sort of–”

“Don’t say it.” Mydei groans.

“--really hot.”

“Phainon.” Mydei replies testily.

“Sorry, I couldn't help myself…” Phainon says sheepishly. “But it’s true, this trinket meant nothing to me. So there’s nothing to feel jealous about. Your gift was more precious than this entire collection combined.”

He supposes that it makes sense. Mydei’s gift had been carefully preserved in a jewelry box, while this one is carelessly strewn over old videogame boxes and other miscellaneous knick-knacks, there’s even a thin layer of dust on it.

Still, he is a petty, possessive thing. That sort of personality trait isn’t exclusive to Phainon alone, and Mydei’s no saint.

“You’ll throw this away, and get rid of anything you’ve received from other exes.”

Phainon nods his head so quickly that his fluffy white hair bounces. “I swear, there’s nothing else, I stopped accepting gifts a long time ago. This probably slipped my radar because I shoved it into my collection and forgot-”

“I will get you a new one.” Mydei has future rockstar money he’s banking on, and a collectible badge is nothing in the grand scheme of things.

Last night, when Cipher and Castorice had been discussing what they’d like to spend their money on once the band took off, Mydei hadn’t been sure of his answer. He’d never been big on material things, didn’t care for private jets, fancy mansions, or expensive cars.

But now, he thinks he’s finally decided on something he would like to spend money on. And that is replacing everything in this apartment that ever came from someone else.

“A better one,” he adds, eyes flickering to Phainon again.

“Okay, I promise.” Phainon kisses him on the cheek sweetly like he’s consoling a child throwing a tantrum. “You’re cute when you’re pouty.”

“That really isn’t… ugh–” Mydei scowls, pushing Phainon away halfheartedly only for the man to latch onto him like a jellyfish again. In the end, he gives up and lets Phainon pull him back to the couch.

He stares at the stack of magazines on the table, most of them containing Phainon’s face, and asks. “Have I ever told you how my family adopted the original Kokopo?”

Phainon seems surprised at this sudden change of topic. “Kokopo? You mean your cat? No.”

“When I was a child, around 7 or 8 years old, I lived in a large house in a wealthy part of Castrum Kremnos. Our neighbour had a child too, a boy,

just a few years younger than me. He was a little spoiled brat who would throw tantrums and let the whole neighbourhood know when he didn’t get his way.”

Phainon tilts his head to the side, confusion plainly written on his face. Despite that he lays his head on Mydei’s shoulder, a silent motion for him to continue.

“He begged and pleaded with his parents for a pet, and after some time, they relented and got him a cat. Cute, tiny, fluffy, stupid looking little creature.”

“He was insufferable about it, took his little minion around and showed it off to everyone he met, including me. But kids like him get bored easily, so after a few weeks I noticed he started neglecting his cat, never played with it, never bought it treats.”

Mydei pauses as Phainon hums to show that he’s listening, idly running his fingers down Mydei’s back through his thin black shirt.

“So I did. I took care of it and treated it like it was my own. Fed it and combed its fur, let it stay over sometimes when it wandered into our yard. I even gave it a name, the Great Beast of Kremnos: Kokopo the 1st.”

“Your neighbour’s kid didn’t mind?” Phainon asks.

“Oh, he minded.” Mydei says, voice smug. “One day the brat saw me feeding Kokopo through the fence and threw a huge fit. Even had his parents come over to speak to mine.”

He looks at Phainon. “Said I shouldn’t interfere with things that didn’t belong to me.”

“Even though I had gotten attached to Kokopo, I knew I had to let it go. I was a good kid who didn’t want to cause any trouble for my parents. I figured that it was just a cat, Kokopo would eventually forget about me if I gave it distance and moved on.”

Phainon is quiet now, his expression thoughtful. His eyes looked sad somehow, like he understands the story a little too well.

“One day, a huge storm ripped through our neighbourhood, tore a hole through the fence. That’s when I saw Kokopo just… standing there, staring at my house. So I thought… what was going to happen if I called out to it.”

Mydei reaches out his hand, laying it on Phainon’s thigh, running his hand down until he reaches his knee. Phainon gulps, eyes flitting downwards as he gets distracted by Mydei’s touch.

“A-and?” He asks shakily. “What happened?”

“I called out to Kokopo, told it I’d let it come back and live with me if it wanted to, and it came running.”

Mydei smiles at the memory. “Of course, I knew a cat wouldn’t understand me. But sometimes I wondered… what if it did?”

Mydei lifts his hand off Phainon’s knee, and the latter whimpers, he gestures for Phainon to come closer, and he unconsciously does.

“The neighbour’s brat, of course, raised hell. He accused me of stealing his cat, his parents even threatened to file a police report against me.”

Phainon is not even aware that his body is practically laying over Mydei’s lap when he asks “What did your parents do about that?”

“Are you kidding? I was also a spoiled brat, of course they took my side.” Mydei says with an amused huff. “They saw the state Kokopo was in when I took him back, and stood by whatever decision I wanted to make.”

Mydei reaches down and runs his fingers through Phainon’s soft, white hair, almost like he’s petting a dog. Phainon finds himself nuzzling into the touch. “And the neighbours?”

“The neighbour’s parents didn’t want to deal with mine, and promised their son they’d get him another present. He didn’t like that outcome, and

actually tried stealing Kokopo back a couple of times until he accidentally broke his arm doing so.”

“...Accidentally?” Phainon repeats.

Mydei smirks down at him, devastating and beautiful. “They could never prove it was me.”

Phainon looks at him like he’s fallen in love all over again.

“Mydei… why have I never heard of this side of you?”

Mydei hums, thinking about it for a moment. “I don’t know. It was so long ago that I forgot until now. I wasn’t proud of what I did, but the kid was a jerk, so he had it coming.”

Mydei continues stroking Phainon’s hair as he cuddles into his lap, happy with the physical closeness. “You see, when Kokopo came back to me, I decided that he was mine.”

“And until the day that he died, Kokopo was my most loyal companion.”

Mydei’s gentle fingers curl into the short wavy strands at the back of Phainon’s head and he tugs, just enough to make Phainon shift his head. The model hardly reacts, too busy looking up at Mydei with hearts in his eyes.

“All that is to say… once I decide that something is mine. I don’t share the things that belong to me.”

Chapter Summary

Mydei’s signature red guitar rests across his lap, his hand caressing the fretboard like a lover. His tight leather pants make his legs look endless as they stretch out beyond the borders of the page.

Phainon is already drooling, and he hasn’t even looked at Mydei’s face yet!

His neck is tilted back over the edge of the chaise, golden eyes looking straight at the camera like he wants to devour the viewer whole. The red crystal pendant hanging off a chain around his neck is held in between his teeth as he smirks at the camera.

Phainon’s throat bobs as he swallows. His saliva feels thick, his legs are weak, his head is swimming. He feels like he’s going to pass out.

“…Do you need to sit down?” He hears Castorice ask.

Sit down? No… no, he needs a defibrillator.

The IPC’s strategic investment department, true to its name, invested in anything that looked likely to make a profit. Properties and large commercial developments were their go-to’s, but their portfolio didn’t stop there. Entertainment, agriculture, professional sports, the list was endless. As long as it could make them money, the IPC wanted their fingers in the pot.

Topaz, as an executive of this department, was tasked with management of their assets to ensure they bore fruit.

It wasn’t always an easy job, but she enjoyed the challenge.

Her most recent acquisition, a rock band called Titans of Calamity, had a lot of promise. And aside from being great at music, they were also really, really good at giving her headaches.

“What do you mean the actor won’t be showing up?” Topaz barks into the phone. The frazzled IPC executive is balancing her laptop on her forearm, while her cellphone is pinched in between her ear and shoulder.

“We booked him weeks in advance!” She grits her teeth, only pausing to hear what the person on the other end has to say.

“A surprise casting call for a Goldweaver campaign? That’s why?” She repeats in disbelief, as though she can’t believe her ears.

“I don’t care if he’s so called ‘perfect for the role’ or if this is a ‘once in a lifetime opportunity’. He was hired for a job and has failed to show up! Unprofessional behaviour will not be tolerated by the IPC. Consider this bridge burned.”

With a growl she abruptly hangs up, her footsteps almost leaving a dust cloud as she storms across the studio.

“The director is going to chew us out again… we’re delayed as it is…” She complains, her hand is gripping her phone so tightly that it seems like it’ll be crushed in her grasp.

Misfortune after misfortune had plagued the Titans of Calamity’s first video shoot until they were delayed by a whole 24 hours. They were supposed to have this wrapped up by yesterday. Acclaimed director Mr Reca’s services did not come cheap, and with the budget she was given, they didn’t have enough to extend filming for another day.

She needs some time to think

We’re taking a short break while I sort things out.” she says to the cast and crew before storming out, her heels making clicking noises as she walks.

Mydei sinks into the nearest chair, grateful for the break after spending nearly the whole day on his feet. It doesn’t take long for Cipher and Castorice to join him, muttering complaints about how their high heels were giving them blisters.

It had been half a year since they put their names down on that contract, signing away their souls to the IPC. From then on, everything had been a whirlwind, things moving at a breakneck pace.

Six months ago, they were playing in shitty dive bars as nobodies with nothing to their name. And now? They have an album, a real studio recorded album that people can hold and listen to. They’ve played gigs on real stages aided by professional stage crews, attended by crowds who actually wanted to be there! They’ve done promotional shoots for brands who actually reached out and wanted their faces on the products. They’re filming a music video right now for their lead single that will even go on television.

Sometimes, it still feels a little insane how quickly their lives changed.

The band's living situation had also improved drastically, the IPC had generously paid for himself, Castorice, and Cipher to move into a bigger, nicer home. They still lived as a trio, because he was used to it, and also because it was more convenient to brainstorm new material this way. But he

would say that yes, having his own ensuite bathroom is a luxury that he could get used to.

Plus, the larger rooms made it easier for his roommates to maintain their sanity when Phainon came over which was… extremely often.

The early days of (re)dating Phainon had been dicey, his friends did not take kindly to Phainon inserting himself back into Mydei’s life.

“What is he doing here?” Cipher had asked the moment she laid eyes on him. “Mydei, why did you bring him into our home?”

In her hand she held one of her fuzzy house slippers, and it was aimed straight at Phainon.

Mydei tried to diffuse the situation, knowing how painful one of those smacks could be. “He insisted on coming up. It’s okay, Cipher, he knew where I lived anyway.”

His reassurance backfired spectacularly when Cipher’s face darkened.

And Phainon, shameless in the worst of ways when it came to Mydei, strided forward with confidence, hand outstretched. “It’s great to meet Mydei’s friends. Greetings. I’m Phainon Khaslana, Mydei’s boyfr-”

Phainon didn’t even get to finish the sentence before the slipper hits him in the forehead with a resounding smack.

It was well deserved. What was not so well deserved was the second slipper that came flying Mydei’s way when he started explaining what had happened the night before and what ‘boyfr-’ entailed.

Cipher refused to let Phainon take a single step into their home for months.

With his trademark persistence Phainon had eventually won her over, or at least made her reluctantly accept the fact that he was part of a combo set with Mydei now. But she still bristled like a cat every time that head of white hair wandered into her peripheral vision.

Even Castorice, Mydei’s number 1 apologist, had been hesitant about his decision. She knew how hurt he’d been by the breakup because she had, unfortunately, seen a lot of the pathetic love songs he wrote in his notebook about ‘nobody in particular’. Still, it didn’t take her long to come around when she saw how Phainon treated him.

“He looks at you like you’re his whole world,” she told him as a response when he asked why she stepped in to mediate when things between Phainon and Cipher got a little heated. “I can’t hate someone who looks at you like that.”

Yeah, she’s too good for this world, too pure. Fame hadn’t changed her at all.

Fame hadn’t changed any of them, really. They had more disposable income now due to the IPC’s generous paychecks, and were recognizable enough to occasionally get stopped on the street for a selfie, but aside from that, the rockstar life isn’t all it’s cracked out to be.

Mostly, it was a lot of work. Long hours crammed in the studio writing songs and crashing out over one note in the chorus that didn’t sound right, take after take in the recording booth ensuring that everything was perfect, not even a breath out of place.

And the fucking meetings!

Mydei thought he would never have to attend one ever again when he walked away from the family business. Well let him just put his clown makeup on because little did he know, he would have to sit in as IPC suits talked about things like ‘market trends’ and ‘building audience anticipation’.

He just wanted to play music, but there was a lot of other bullshit that came with it.

Album launches, listening parties, small intimate gigs for the superfans, cryptic social media posts to build up hype, press interviews. The IPC poured money in, and they expected to collect it all back—with interest.

Like Topaz said on the day she signed them, the IPC doesn’t make deals that don’t pay off. They saw potential in Mydei’s band, and were going all in until they hit it big or collapsed under the pressure, whichever came first.

And while the Titans of Calamity were prepared for hardship—this was their dream and none of them were letting go without a fight—it didn’t change the fact that it was exhausting.

“If I have to hear this song one more time, I’m going to lose my mind.” Cipher complains, putting a finger gun to her head and miming pulling the trigger. She lights a cigarette, even though she knows she shouldn’t be smoking indoors.

Mydei’s eyes track the thin trail of smoke as it floats upwards, and he thinks, fair. He didn’t know much about the music industry prior to joining it, and had no idea that artists didn’t sing or play their instruments live while filming a video, that everything was lipsynced to the recording, and that it took days to complete a single 4 minute music video. Redoing the same takes from multiple angles, repeating the same scene over and over until it was perfect.

Their lead single, which they had been so proud of, had been playing on loop until he’d started to hate the sound of his own voice. And this was only the beginning.

“Better get used to it,” he says. “You heard Topaz. Lead single means we’re stuck playing it in every set for the foreseeable future.”

“It’s a good song,” Castorice says, closing her eyes with a blissful expression like she had accepted her fate. “I think I was sick of it yesterday, but today, I’m coming back around to loving it.”

Cipher takes a long drag of her cigarette and exhales, smoke rings forming in the air.

“May we all match your level of insanity soon,” she sighs.

“Hyacine taught me something the other day…” Castorice hums thoughtfully. “She said, if you’re going through rough times, sometimes it helps to take a moment to realign, remind ourselves why we’re doing this.”

Yeah… Mydei seemed to recall her saying something like that. Something cheesy about staying grounded, and remembering what really matters.

He shrugs. “Worth a shot.”

“Why the fuck not?” Cipher murmurs, leaning forward in her seat.

Castorice looks pleased as the band huddles into a circle, putting their heads close together like a pre-show ritual. “Then on the count of three, let’s each shout out the one thing that keeps us going.”

“Fine.” “Whatever.”

Mydei and Cipher didn’t sound delighted about it, but at least they weren’t complaining as Castorice counted cheerfully “One… two…three!”

“The fans!” she says enthusiastically.

“The music.” Mydei says dryly.

And then a sharp voice cuts through both of theirs as Cipher yells at the top of her lungs.

“FOR THE MONEY!”

Mydei and Castorice fall silent, staring at her in wide-eyed shock.

“What?” She turns to address them. “You two need to get your priorities in order, or this industry will eat you alive.”

Mydei snorts despite himself. It was a little ridiculous, but he does feel a little bit better. He appreciates all they’re doing for him, his bandmates, colleagues, and best friends.

He relaxes in his seat, tunes out the sound of their conversation as he checks his phone. Phainon had been busy all day with a shoot but he should be done about now… right on cue, there are notifications for new messages on his screen.

Puppy Finally finished the shoot! ヽ(・∀・)ﾉ Are you guys still filming?

Mydei We’re delayed again Background actor didn’t show up

Not looking good

Puppy Huuuh? (＃`Д´) I’m on my way will be there soon. Have you eaten? Are you hungry? Nvm I’ll grab your favourite Kremnoan takeaway on the way ( ´ ▽ ` )

Mydei It’s fine, I’m not hungry

Puppy Don’t worry me like this… I noticed that you haven’t been meeting your protein intake for the past 2 days And you drank coffee this morning, you hate coffee!

Mydei

? We didn’t see each other today

Puppy One of the staff members tried to be clever by sneaking a shot of you on stellargram. I already reported it. You looked tired, I didn’t like it.

Mydei

HKS

He eyes the three dots that indicate Phainon is typing.

“That’s enough!” Cipher snatches his phone away like he’s a toddler with too much screen time. “Always on your phone texting your boyfriend, you haven’t even listened to a word I said! Put down your phone and talk to someone. Geez, you’re becoming as much of a hermit as Princess Homebody.”

Castorice yelps as she catches strays while Mydei just stares at Cipher with an unimpressed expression.

“You know that’s not true, you just have a vendetta against Phainon. Give it back.”

“No,” Cipher clutches his phone with both hands and holds it behind her back, out of his reach. “You two are going to learn how to live apart. Don’t make me throw away your phone.”

Mydei crosses his arms, narrowing his eyes as he sizes her up. “Try it, he has a tracking app installed, so he’ll just find it anyway.”

Cipher throws the phone into his lap like it’s a poisonous frog. “What the fuck is wrong with you two!”

Well, true, he realizes the relationship he has with Phainon isn’t exactly normal. Sometimes, Mydei wonders if he had gone too easy on him when he agreed to get back together. He should have been a little more cautious,

held back a little, made him work for it. He’d been too caught up in the moment, he supposed, and his judgment slipped.

Phainon had taken it as permission to speed run the relationship, he moved fast. Gifts, blowing up his phone 24/7 with messages, romantic gestures both big and small, his commitment to the craft was terrifying. Mydei’s roommates still brought up the ‘Hyacinth incident’, where he stood outside their home in the rain for 2 hours holding a bouquet of hyacinths just to commemorate Mydei’s 5th consecutive loss to him in some stupid video game competition they were having.

He was intense, Mydei will give him that. The protagonists of romance movies had nothing on him. He was insecure in ways that he never showed to anyone but Mydei. Like a needy dog, prone to spiralling into despair if Mydei was too busy to give him attention. And sometimes, he could be suffocating in the way he hovered around him, like he was scared Mydei would forget about him as soon as he turned his back.

But to Mydei, falling in love with Phainon was the easiest thing in the world. In fact, he didn’t think he’d ever stopped being in love with him. Mydei loved all of him, even the parts that were a little too much. It was exactly what he wanted, and he wasn’t about to complain about his steak being too juicy, his lobster too buttery.

Sure, it was a little eerie when Phainon knew things about him that Mydei never shared, and he had an uncanny ability to read his mind even before his thoughts could fully form. He thinks Phainon does it to prove that he’s the only one who knows him inside and out.

But eh, Mydei was slowly getting used to it.

“It was a compromise we agreed on,” he told Cipher. “After I ghosted him for hours when we had that listening party last month.”

She looked at him like he had lost his mind. “Why would you–nevermind, I don’t know what goes on in your pretty little head. I’ve never seen someone have such a bad crashout over a few missed calls. It wasn’t even your fault, the line was shitty.”

Mydei shrugs. “He was fine.”

Cipher gives him a look. “No he wasn’t. I actually feared for your life when he dragged you into the recording room.”

Mydei smirks when he remembers the memory. Phainon, nearly delirious with worry, pushing him against the wall and having his way with him. The dark look on his face had been so hot as he failed to keep his composure.

“Stop.” Cipher immediately says, “Whatever you’re thinking about just. Stop. I don’t want to know what you did that day.”

“He was upset, wasn’t he?” Castorice asks, trying and failing to hide her obvious curiosity. “Was he jealous?”

“Cas, no.” Cipher puts her hands over her ears.

“Would you say it was more a subtle, simmering jealousy, or the intense, explosive kind?” Mydei doesn’t answer that, which only made her eyes shine brighter.

“Oh, I see. And after that, would you say you blissfully made out or was it like… rougher?” Castorice continues, procuring a notebook out of nowhere, she’d been carrying it around with her a lot lately, calling it ‘journalling’.

“Little lion, I’ll kill you if you answer that,” Cipher snaps.

Mydei shakes his head with a small smile, looking back at his phone. According to his messages, Phainon was on his way with an ETA of 10 minutes.

He didn’t know why Phainon had been so insistent on showing up to the video shoot. He still worked as a full time model, and was always busy. The actor is supposed to be an ordinary guy dressed in a crisp white shirt and a black tie that Mydei allows to approach him. It’s a classic trope, the fantasy between a rockstar and an ordinary fan.

“Is our last minute actor ready?” Mr Reca hollers at the dressing room “Everybody’s waiting for him.”

“Just finishing hair and makeup, director!” A staff member replies as Phainon walks out onto the set.

And Mydei’s breath catches in his throat.

Fuck him.

Phainon is obviously… not that. There is no universe where he can ever be considered ‘plain’ or ‘nondescript’ even though the hair and makeup crew had tried their best.

A collared white shirt that doesn’t fit him properly, plain black slacks and neck tie in a perfect Windsor knot. The thick black rimmed glasses look comically fake the way they stand out against his face, the lenses so thick that Mydei can hardly see his blue eyes. His hair’s been mussed up deliberately, bangs covering almost half his face.

It’s so different from the way Mydei is used to seeing him. And it’s unfair that Phainon still looks this good despite all efforts made to dim his light.

Phainon always knew exactly how to drive him insane.

And now Mydei can only stare, gobsmacked, as his boyfriend walks towards him; heat curling in his abdomen, cock stirring in his pants. None of which is decidedly professional behaviour.

Mr Reca motions for the cameras to start rolling. “Take one. Mydeimos, you know what to do. Khaslana, as we discussed earlier, follow the script. Now… action!” He snaps the clapperboard as the song starts playing from the speakers.

The original idea was for Mydei to ignore the actor as he approaches, playing the part of a nonchalant rockstar. But this time, he can’t help but look up when footsteps approach him. Phainon’s shadow envelopes him, the angling and lighting making his already impressive frame look even broader. The lines between the pursuer and the pursued are getting blurry.

“How do I look?” Phainon mouths playfully, lips curled up in a shit eating grin as he places a knee on the sofa, right next to where Mydei is sitting. Like this, he’s almost straddling him. He’s close, closer than Mydei expected him to be, closer than he planned for. If Phainon leans forward just a little bit more, the tips of his messy white hair would touch Mydei’s face. “Do you like me like this?”

The answer is yes, pathetically so, soppingly so. But Phainon’s head is big enough without him stroking his ego even more. Someone needs to push him down a peg or two.

“You look stupid.”  Mydei mouths back, making sure to enunciate every word.

Phainon snorts, tilting his head to the side so that his hair brushes his shoulder. Whatever he’s thinking about, he seems to come to a conclusion when he snorts and flashes Mydei a smile, white teeth peeking through pale lips. Mydei watches him mouth a singular word.

“Okay.”

What’s that supposed to mean?

All of a sudden, Phainon darts forward quickly, like he’s trying to shove Mydei down. They don’t touch, but Mydei goes down like a stack of cards anyway, sideways until his back is pressing against the seat of the couch. Caught off guard, Mydei reaches and grabs the end of Phainon’s neck tie.

“What are you doing?” Mydei asks. He’s going off script, but that is the least of his concerns as his words come out in a panic. They are muffled by the loud music, but they’re close enough that he’s sure Phainon can hear him. He’s vaguely aware of the fact that he’s probably wide-eyed from shock, losing control of the situation.

“Nothing. Just playing my part.” Phainon’s voice is cocky, teasing. He’s so close that Mydei can feel his warm breath on his cheek when he speaks close to his ear, and Mydei instinctively shivers. “Why are you so scared suddenly? I thought you rehearsed this.”

Mydei exhales shakily, his body is on fire. He itches to lay his hands on Phainon, to run his fingers down over the contours of his body and feel the muscle flex beneath that thin white shirt. He’s so turned on right now but he can’t let it show, and it’s taking every ounce of discipline he has just to stay sane.

It would be easy for him to stay professional and just do his job if the other party is an actor whom he doesn’t know and has no feelings for. But it’s a whole different ball game when it’s his sexy, handsome, insanely attractive supermodel boyfriend leaning down over him. His restraint can only go so far before it snaps like a thread.

“Relax,” Phainon murmurs into his ear as Mydei’s body tenses in a way that’s anything but. “Anything he can do, I can do better~ I’ll make you look so good.”

Mydei scoffs with the belated realization that Phainon is somehow competing with a faceless, nameless person neither of them had ever met. But of course he had no doubt that Phainon would emerge victorious, that was as obvious as saying that the sky is blue.

Meanwhile the song is still blaring in the background and Mydei knows he needs to focus. The next verse is starting, and he seems to recall that he should be doing something with it but finds that all rational thought has flown out of his head when Phainon smirks down at him like that.

Glasses tilted low enough to see the blue of his eyes as he peers over them, fluffy white bangs falling over his forehead. His shirt is tailored for a much smaller man, and of course there was no time to get one that actually fits. The white fabric stretches tightly over his broad shoulders, tapers his narrow waist. When his torso shifts and the shirt moves, smooth skin and defined muscle peek out from the gaps where the buttons fail to do their job.

Their thighs touch as Phainon moves closer, brushing against Mydei’s on accident. Touching was not in the script, but it was natural for mistakes to happen when two people were in such close proximity.

Well… ‘mistakes’.

The set fills with noise again as the crew bustles to get themselves in position for a retake.

Mydei glares at Phainon accusingly, this is all his fault. He made Mydei lose focus.

The infuriating man just smiles at him, fully knowing the effect he has on Mydei. “Try not to get distracted this time,” he says in a sing-song voice.

In response, Mydei spitefully wraps the necktie around his knuckle and tugs, pulling Phainon forward until their noses almost touch. Even though he’d been at work all day, Phainon smells so good, musky cedarwood mingling with the gentle scent of peaches.

“Let’s hurry it up, think I’m starting to hate this song,” Mydei grumbles, now that he’s listening to it for the billionth time, everything sounds so embarrassing. The lyrics are corny and the way his vocals dip low at the end of the line sounds so fucking forced. It’s starting to not even sound like his voice at all.

He’s definitely not thinking about how close Phainon is to him, how his breath tickles when he leans against him like that. How close his hand is hovering over his skin that he can feel the warmth radiating off his palm. How Phainon’s stray hairs get blown around by the breeze and how the white strands sparkle when the light hits it. Cause what we do in the dark has got me thinking

Honestly, Mydei is pretty much at his limit too, he’s overstimulated to the point of pain, his insides rubbed raw. Through the haze of lust crowding his thoughts he barely has the energy to nod weakly, but that is all the confirmation Phainon needs.

He can feel the moment Phainon absolutely crumbles. When his body shudders violently and he collapses his entire weight on top of Mydei as he orgasms, forgetting how to support his own weight. The way he cries Mydei’s name sounds like a prayer, a fervent declaration of his devotion.

It’s followed by a feeling that is now familiar to Mydei, the sensation of being completely filled to the brim.

And then they both just lie there for a bit. Spent, exhausted, and utterly satisfied.

Mydei is aware of nothing but the movement of his own chest as he breathes in and out, trying to recirculate oxygen to his body. His muscles ache pleasantly, limbs boneless, thoughts dragging along sluggishly through the haze. Above him, Phainon’s body lies limp and heavy, a deadweight.

Every now and again, his muscles twitch as though recalling the feeling of coming over and over again.

Mydei just sighs and throws his head back onto the soft fabrics that cushion their bodies, the smell of sex still lingering in the air. And in that moment, he feels so cozy and appeased that he could probably fall asleep right then and there.

The shuffling of footsteps outside quickly pulls him back into reality. Right, there were crew members staying late, probably cleaning up. The problem with having sex in an area that anyone could easily access at any time means that falling asleep directly afterwards isn’t an option.

“We… we should get going.” Mydei reluctantly pushes Phainon off him, aching muscles protesting at the movement. They’re not the only ones protesting, because the way Phainon whines as he pulls out makes it sound like he’s been asked to do something impossible. Immediately, Mydei feels empty, missing the warmness and closeness of before.

If they were in the comfort of their own home, sometimes he’d let Phainon keep it in a little longer after sex. Just… let him stay there and maybe fall asleep with Phainon inside him. Cockwarming feels nice, intimate, just comfortable, a sign of their love and trust for each other.

It’s times like these where he yearns for a home with Phainon more than anything. Somewhere that is truly theirs, somewhere where they didn’t have to hold themselves back from showing affection, somewhere where Phainon can freely cling to Mydei like an oversized dog.

He’d even tolerate seeing Phainon’s freaky ass collection of Mydei’s merchandise, life sized cutout and all, if that’s what it would take.

“Phainon…” Mydei murmurs softly. “Let’s go home.”

Phainon just smiles dopily at him, expression totally blissed out.

“Okay.”

Mydei’s memories of arriving home are hazy at best. He vaguely remembers Phainon lugging his very large, very sleepy, and very annoyed ass into the car. Then out of the car, into Mydei’s apartment, then into his shower where he leaned against the cubicle half asleep as Phainon washed his hair for him.

Luckily for them, they didn’t run into anybody along the way. No exasperated Cipher sideeyeing their PDA, no curious Castorice collecting more material for her journal. It seemed like the girls were equally exhausted after working so hard and had turned in early for the night.

It’s not until they’re both tucked into Mydei’s soft, warm, king-sized bed, Phainon latching onto him with all four limbs like some oversized octopus when Phainon circles back to a topic he thought they had dropped.

“So… who’s been telling you that you’re so cute that they could eat you up?”

Mydei snorts in laughter before he can help himself.

“You think this is funny?” Phainon tightens his hold on him until he can’t even move, and he can practically hear the pout in his voice. “I asked you a question, Mydeimos.”

“She was a single mother who went back to college after having her 2nd kid, Phainon. I don’t think you have to worry about her.”

He feels Phainon’s shoulders sag in relief, and a soft thump as he presses his face in Mydei’s back, between his shoulderblades.

“Thank the gods…” he sighs.

Ridiculous crisis averted, for now. But this is probably something that needed to be addressed, and now’s as good a time as any.

“You’ve been acting strange lately,” Mydei brings up, feeling Phainon stiffen behind him, followed by obnoxiously fake laughter.

“Is that so?”

“Yeah,” stranger than usual, at least. Phainon had always been a little weird. “You know, if you’re not okay with the photoshoot concepts, all you had to do was say something.”

There is a pause, and he feels Phainon’s arms tighten around his waist followed by a soft, timid ‘I know....”

Phainon continues meekly. “I just didn’t want to seem like I was too jealous or controlling. I want to support you in your career.”

Mydei feels his heart melt, how adorable is this man?

“Trust me,” He brushes his thumb against Phainon’s hands, which are tightly linked together in front of his bellybutton. “I feel plenty supported by you.”

These days, he even dreads stepping into Phainon’s penthouse because of all the Mydei merch he owns. He’s starting to suspect that his boyfriend may have a hoarding problem.

“Besides,” Mydei continues. “I like that you get jealous… It makes me feel like you really want me.”

Phainon is quiet for a little while, but when he speaks again his voice is light, tinged with an undercurrent of hurt and insecurity that he can’t fully hide. “The hundred times I talk about you everyday still doesn’t make you feel like I want you?”

Mydei rolls his eyes, Phainon is a HKS to the core. Six months of dating and he’s still insecure about their relationship? But it’s not like Mydei can blame him, since the scars of their past were not so easily healed. It’s all they can do to comfort each other in small, tender moments like these, to reassure that the love was reciprocated.

Mydei rolls on the bed, turning to look at Phainon face to face. Without saying a word, he tucks the loose locks of white hair behind his ears.

They’re still slightly damp from where Phainon hadn’t dried his hair properly, very soft to touch, and small faintly of his own strawberry shampoo.

He starts to feel a little bit bad at the sight of Phainon’s crestfallen expression. “Sorry, that’s not what I meant. I just didn’t think that you from 6 months ago would be okay with me doing these sorts of shoots so part of me just wanted to… push you a little.”

It kind of sounds worse when he airs it out in the open like that.

And Phainon catches on quickly.

“Mydeimos,” Phainon says, propping himself up on a single elbow. “If I didn’t know any better, I’d think you were accepting these jobs on purpose to test me.”

Heat immediately flows to Mydei’s face. It’s not like he was going out of his way to do so… the IPC had pitched these as legitimate marketing strategies, and refusing it would have made all of their jobs significantly more difficult.

But… maybe… okay, maybe there was a part of him that wanted to see Phainon get a little bit jealous.

Phainon unlatches his fingers only to dig them into the dips above Mydei’s hips and squeeze lightly, a threat. Ever since discovering that Mydei was ticklish, he had used his powers for evil, to devastating effect.

He jabs a finger into the flesh under his ribs, and that’s enough to make Mydei’s entire body jolt.

“Well? Were you?” Phainon asks again, faux innocently. He wriggles his fingers into Mydei’s tender flesh again and Mydei nearly throws him off the bed this time.

Mydei just glares at him, face feeling hot and flushed. He doesn’t want to admit the truth, that would be too embarrassing, but he doesn’t want to lie

either, so Mydei opts for a third option and changes the subject completely.

“I saw something interesting when browsing your fanpages the other day,” he starts casually.

Phainon stops tickling him to literally cringe when he mentions the fanpages.

“Come on…” he says sheepishly. “Stop browsing those tabloids. You know I’ll tell you everything you want to know.”

“Humph, only if you stop buying my merch. I can’t even take 10 steps into your house without seeing my face everywhere.”

“So you can be a creepy fanboy but I can’t do the same?” Phainon protests, Mydei ignores him because he does not want to acknowledge the hypocrisy that he also runs his own fan account for Phainon.

A fan account that, by the way, broke a hundred thousand followers just last week, an impressive milestone. People online loved it because it always somehow managed to get shots of the elusive model that nobody else was able to, something different than the usual blurry walking snapshot taken off the street. Gym selfies, pictures of Phainon mid-nap, exclusive behind the scenes shots at a photoshoot. Netizens often speculated that it was Phainon’s own management running the account to generate hype but the real reason… is Mydei’s little secret.

Mydei lifts up his phone from its charger, the black screen flashing to life when he opens it to show Phainon the bookmarked posts of him out and about, captured by his competitors (other fanpages). There is a familiar pink-haired woman walking next to him, their arms linked together by the elbow.

Scrolling through the comments, opinions varied, but most seemed to speculate that they were dating.

Phainon just blinks at the pictures, like he hadn’t expected to be caught in the act. “Wait, wait wait wait– Cyrene was just–”

“I’m not accusing her,” Mydei says flatly, shutting down that train of thought. “She was the one who called me first.” He remembered picking up the phone thinking there was an emergency due to how panicked she was, only to find out she was just desperate to prevent a misunderstanding before it happened.

“You’re the best thing that’s ever happened to Phainon,” She told him fervently. “Those years where you were broken up he was just so… so wrong. I’ll do anything I can to avoid that outcome again.”

He adored Cyrene, his initial impressions of her had been completely wrong. Once he got to know her a little bit more, he found out she was kind, thoughtful, funny, an amazing friend, and they got along wonderfully. It wasn’t long before she became one of his most trusted confidantes.

“You could have told me if you were looking for jewelry. I could have gone with you.” It’s a bit hurtful because Phainon of all people knows how much Mydei loves jewelry. Rings, necklaces, earrings, he’s rarely seen without wearing some of it on his person, and his entire fashion sense revolves around accessories. What? Is Mydei’s taste not good enough for him or something? Like Phainon’s taste in clothing is any better? Those t-shirts he always wears are atrocious.

Mydei raises an eyebrow. “But I guess we shouldn’t be seen together in public going jewelry shopping.”

Their public relationship is a contentious subject, and it turns into an argument every time it’s brought up. Logically, he knows why their relationship should be kept secret, and it makes sense. Mydei’s career is still tenuous, one wrong move might turn into a scandal that mars his reputation, but the one he’s really worried about is Phainon.

Phainon with his passionate fanbase, Phainon with his squeaky clean public image. He thought he’d grown out of the mindset, but a part of Mydei couldn't help but fear that he wasn’t good enough. That people would still look at the two of them and think why the hell Phainon would date someone like him.

It seemed… easier to just avoid the topic altogether, so that’s why he continues to insist on keeping their relationship secret. Even though Phainon has made it clear that it’s not what he wants.

Phainon flushes pink for some unknown reason. “No… you’re misunderstanding, it’s not because of that I… argh…” he groans, running a hand through his hair.

“?” Mydei’s confusion is almost audible in the darkness.

“I was kind of hoping to keep it a secret for a little while longer,” he finally admits.

And Mydei admits that he is totally lost. “A secret that you went jewelry shopping?”

Why does that even need to be a secret?

Then he sighs, quietly hurt but letting it slide. He shouldn’t be pushy. Phainon has always been honest with him and will tell him the reasoning when he is ready. He shouldn’t be jealous either, but sometimes the intensity of his own feelings rage violent and terrifying, like a wave he can’t tame.

But that isn’t Phainon’s problem, it’s his, so Mydei has to do his best to control his own emotions.

“Sorry,” he says. “I shouldn’t have pushed. Good night, Phainon.” And with that, he turns himself so that he faces away from Phainon and tries to go to sleep.

“Hey, hey. I’m not done talking.” Phainon can get really pushy when he wants to be, and there is no subtlety in the way he grabs Mydei’s shoulder and flips him over like he’s nothing more than a pancake until they’re so close that their noses almost touch.

Mydei just waits quietly for him to speak as Phainon’s face gets redder and redder. His boyfriend licks his lips, uncharacteristically nervous.

“I… I was looking at rings.” Phainon says after a moment, voice so soft it can barely be considered a whisper.

Mydei squints, thinking he’d misheard. “Come again?”

Phainon’s gaze darts to the side. “I know that we’ve not been together for very long, but I was going to ask you to marry me. It kills me that we can’t make our relationship public, I understand the reasoning, but… it would make me feel better if you wore my ring, so that people knew you were taken.”

Mydei blinks, his chest feeling all warm and tingly all of a sudden. Phainon had already thought that far ahead?

Marriage… Mydei had never thought too deeply about it, it always seemed like something that was out of his reach. His parents were happily married and adored each other deeply, and sure Mydei had hoped he could obtain something similar for himself one day but it’s just…

He just… never really let himself linger upon it, that’s all.

“You really want to marry me?” He’s not prepared for how fragile and vulnerable his voice sounds, like he’s on the verge of tears.

“Of course,” Phainon says warmly. “You didn’t think I’d spend all those years chasing you only to let you go, did you? Marriage would bind us together, forever.”

He takes Mydei’s hand and holds it, pressing his fingernail against the base of Mydei’s ring finger until it hurts. When he lets go, there is an indentation of fingernail marks at the position where a wedding band would sit.

“Because you’d have to swear an oath to me too, and I know you’ll never break a promise.” Phainon continues.

Mydei’s lip curls up into a smile. “You don’t need marriage for me to surrender my heart to you when it has always been yours. And I don’t see why you can’t have the rest of me for the rest of our lives too.”

He’d always been a man filled with certainty, and this is no exception. “I would choose you over and over again.”

Phainon mirrors his smile, teeth shining bright in the darkness.

“You are so…” He appears so moved that he can’t even finish his sentence. “Well… it will take me some time to formally propose, not any old proposal would do, you know? You deserve something incredible. As for the engagement ring… maybe something to match the sun brooch you got me…”

Mydei clicks his tongue, it’s always embarrassing whenever he brings up that silly teenage gift as though Mydei hasn’t gotten him anything nicer since they started dating. “HKS, stop bringing that up.”

Phainon laughs cheerfully, bright and relieved before leaning in to kiss him. It’s not one of those desperate kisses that tries to eat him alive, this one is gentle, soft. It doesn’t turn him on or make heat shoot down his loins; it just feels… good, right, perfect even. It feels like Mydei could kiss him forever.

And what’s stopping him from doing so? Nothing.

“You took tomorrow off, right?” Mydei asks as Phainon lazily pulls away from him.

“Of course,” he chirps cheerfully. “It’s your first day off in forever. It’s been too long since we went on a date, just you and me.”

“Let’s go shop for rings together,” Mydei suggests abruptly. “I don’t want to wait anymore.”

Phainon gapes and he nearly chokes on his own saliva, pale eyelashes fluttering as he blinks frantically. “What?”

“Can’t let you go and choose something terrible for me.” Mydei says, like it’s a foregone conclusion.

“But the tabloids–”

“Are going to have a field day.”

“--And the IPC–”

“Are going to be so pissed off and there would be nothing they can do about it.” He genuinely likes Topaz and is sorry for all the extra work that he's going to put on her. But not sorry enough to change his mind.

Phainon still looks unconvinced. “But my fans, your career–”

“Are going to be fine.” Mydei tells him firmly. “Or do you not trust me to have everything under control?”

“No, of course I trust you,” Reassured by his words, or perhaps the utter confidence in the way he declares it, Phainon’s unease melts away. The smile is back, more blinding than ever, so bright it could light up the entire room.

Mydei thinks he looks best this way, at ease and smiling, happy and healthy, no trace of despair or loneliness in his blue eyes.

With a smile that shines as brightly as the sun.

Mydei’s own personal sunshine.

~The End~
